The Netjes package's `build/Netjes.targets`, imported into every project that references it, runs `npm run build` during publish (`vite build && vite build --ssr` in the template) and ships `dist/` with the app:

- `dist/client/`: the browser's JavaScript and CSS, content-hashed under `assets/`, and the files from `public/`, with Vite's manifest in `.vite/`.
- `dist/server/`: the server bundle the Node processes import, with React and every other dependency bundled in, and the sidecar script (`netjes-sidecar.mjs`).

The published folder runs without `node_modules`. Three MSBuild properties change what publish does:

| Property | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `NetjesSkipClientBuild` | unset | `true` publishes a `dist/` that is already built, for a CI step or Docker stage that builds the client on its own. |
| `NetjesBuildCommand` | `npm run build` | The command that builds the client. |
| `NetjesRoot` | the project's folder | Where `package.json` and `dist/` are. |

`netjes build` does the client build on its own (it also writes the generated types first), and `netjes start` runs the app in Production from the project or a published `.dll` (run from the `.dll`'s folder). See the [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/cli.md).

## What the server needs

- The ASP.NET Core runtime, 10.0.14 or newer.
- Node.js `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0` (Node.js 22.22.2 or a later 22, 24.15.0 or a later 24, or 26 or newer), as `node` on the path (or `NetjesOptions.NodeExecutable`). Netjes starts the Node processes itself; you do not run them.
- The published folder, with `dist/`. In Production the app reads `dist/client/.vite/manifest.json` at startup and stops when it is missing.

The app runs in Production mode whenever the environment is not Development (`ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT`); `Netjes:Mode` sets the mode outright.

When the app finds no build, or cannot start Node.js, it says so in one line and exits with code 1. It logs the reason as a critical entry, the last thing it logs, with what to do:

```text
crit: Netjes.Rendering.ViteManifestProvider[0]
      No production build found at '/app/dist/client/.vite/manifest.json'. To develop, run `npm run dev`, or start the app with ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development. To run in production, build first: `npm run build` in '/app'.
```

For Node.js the line is `Could not start 'node'. Is Node.js installed and on the PATH? Set Netjes:NodeExecutable to use another executable.`, and for a build without the sidecar script `` Cannot find the netjes sidecar at '/app/dist/server/netjes-sidecar.mjs'. Run `npm run build` in '/app'. ``. A container runtime or process manager sees exit code 1, as for any app that fails to start. In a test host such as `WebApplicationFactory`, the start fails with that message instead ([testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/testing.md#the-app-over-http)).

## Docker

Every app made with `netjes new` has a `Dockerfile` and three Compose files. An app scaffolded from a Netjes checkout references that checkout instead of the packages, and the Docker build cannot see the checkout, so pass `--packages` there.

```bash
docker compose up                                                     # development: dotnet watch + Vite HMR on http://localhost:8080
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d  # the production image
```

The `Dockerfile` has these stages:

| Stage | What it does |
|---|---|
| `deps` | `npm ci`, cached until `package.json` or the lockfile changes. |
| `dev` | The .NET SDK with Node, running `dotnet watch run`; the source is bind-mounted. |
| `client` | `npm run build`: `dist/client` and `dist/server`. |
| `build` | `dotnet publish` with `-p:NetjesSkipClientBuild=true`, taking `dist/` from `client`. |
| `production` | The ASP.NET Core runtime image plus the `node` binary, the published app, running as the non-root `app` user, with a `HEALTHCHECK` on `/healthz`. |

The Compose files:

- `docker-compose.yml` defines the `app` service from the `production` stage, with `pull_policy: build`, so `up -d` always builds and never reuses a stale or development image.
- `docker-compose.override.yml`, which Compose loads by default, switches to the `dev` stage, bind-mounts the source, and publishes ports 8080 and 5173 on `127.0.0.1` only: development error pages show stack traces and Vite serves the source.
- `docker-compose.prod.yml` publishes port 8080 and runs the container read-only, with a `tmpfs` at `/tmp`, `no-new-privileges`, every capability dropped, limits of one CPU and 512 MB, `restart: always`, and a named volume for ASP.NET Core's Data Protection keys, which sign antiforgery tokens and the draft mode cookie, so they survive restarts and new images.

ASP.NET Core logs a warning at startup that those keys are not encrypted at rest. Encrypt them with one of the `ProtectKeysWith...` methods (a certificate, Azure Key Vault) if that matters where you run.

## Configuration

`NetjesOptions` binds from the `Netjes` configuration section, so any ASP.NET Core configuration source sets it: `appsettings.json`, `appsettings.Production.json`, environment variables (`Netjes__SidecarProcesses=4`, `Netjes__Images__RemoteHosts__0=images.example.com`), the command line. Code in `AddNetjes(options => ...)` runs after the binding and wins.

```json
{
  "AllowedHosts": "shop.example",
  "Netjes": {
    "SidecarProcesses": 4,
    "Images": { "RemoteHosts": ["images.example.com"] },
    "PublicConfig": { "ApiBase": "https://api.shop.example" }
  }
}
```

`Netjes:PublicConfig` is sent to the browser as it is and read with `usePublicConfig()`, so the same build runs in every environment (see [data loading](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md)). Every option and key is in the [options reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/options.md).

Startup work the CLI's `generate` and `routes` commands do not need, such as migrating a database, can be skipped with `app.GetNetjesCommand()`:

```csharp
if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment() && app.GetNetjesCommand() is null)
{
    await Database.MigrateAndSeedAsync(app.Services);
}
```

## Sizing

- `SidecarProcesses` (default 1) sets how many Node processes render pages. A process renders one document at a time on one core, so an app whose pages take real CPU time to render wants about one per core. Client navigations do not use them. See [rendering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/rendering-and-streaming.md#the-sidecar-pool).
- The image endpoint's memory is bounded by its settings, roughly `MaxConcurrency` × (2 × `MaxSourceBytes` + 4 bytes × the processor's `MaxPixels`) + `MaxRemoteFetches` × `MaxSourceBytes`. Lower them in small containers; see [images](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/images.md).
- The output cache's `SizeLimit` (100 MB by default) bounds the memory of the in-memory store.

## Several instances

Behind a load balancer, any instance may answer any request, including each client navigation of one visitor. The instances need to share three things, and a rolling deploy runs two builds side by side for a while.

### The Data Protection key ring

Authentication cookies, antiforgery tokens and the draft mode cookie are protected with ASP.NET Core Data Protection. Give every instance the same application name and a key ring they all read, as for any ASP.NET Core app behind a load balancer:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddDataProtection()
    .SetApplicationName("MyApp")
    .PersistKeysToFileSystem(new DirectoryInfo("/keys")); // or a database, Redis, Azure Blob Storage
```

### The output-cache store

Cached pages use ASP.NET Core output caching, whose default store is in memory, per instance. Each instance then renders and stores its own copy of a page, and `Revalidate`, `RevalidatePath` and `IPageCache` evict only on the instance that ran them. Register a store the instances share, such as Redis (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.OutputCaching.StackExchangeRedis`):

```csharp
builder.Services.AddStackExchangeRedisOutputCache(options => options.Configuration = "redis:6379");
builder.Services.AddOutputCache();
```

Then an entry stored by one instance is served by the others on the same build (for payloads that reuse a layout, only with the same secret, below), and revalidating on one evicts for all. Signed-in visitors are never served or stored either way.

### The segment key secret

On client navigations the router sends the keys of the layouts it holds (`X-Netjes-Segments`), and the server skips the layout loaders whose key is unchanged. Keys are signed with `NetjesOptions.SegmentKeySecret`, which is random per process by default, so a key one instance issued means nothing to another: that instance loads the layout in full.

The output cache keys a client payload by which layouts the visitor holds a valid key for. A payload that reuses a layout is also keyed by a fingerprint of the secret (never the secret itself), because it names the visitor's key, and only instances with the same secret accept it. Documents and full payloads reuse nothing, so every instance on the store shares them, whatever its secret.

With the default secret, then, a layout is reused only when the instance that signed the visitor's key answers, and each instance stores its own payloads that reuse a layout. To reuse layouts on every instance and share those entries, set the same secret everywhere, at least 32 bytes, kept out of source control like any secret:

```bash
openssl rand -base64 32                  # once
Netjes__SegmentKeySecret=<that value>    # in every instance's environment
```

Changing the secret makes the keys that clients hold unknown, so their next navigation loads its layouts in full, and leaves the entries stored under the old one to expire.

### Rolling deploys

While a deploy replaces instances one by one, instances on the old and the new build answer side by side and share the store. Every cached page is keyed by the client build, the version of the Vite build the instance serves, so neither serves the other's entries: a document names its own build's assets, which instances on the other build may not have, and a payload from another build makes the client load the page again. Each build renders and stores its own copies, so the new build starts with an empty cache, and the old build's entries expire on their own.

A visitor whose browser runs the old build and whose navigation reaches a new instance gets the new build's payload, so the browser loads that page as a new document; there is nothing to configure for that. Until the deploy completes, a load balancer that spreads one visitor's requests over both builds can send that document, or a later navigation, to the other build again, and each switch loads the page anew. Sticky sessions avoid that.

### Size and hosts

A cached page's entry is keyed on the host, the path and query string as sent, and the client build, and the cache's size limit counts bodies, not keys. Pin `AllowedHosts` and bound the store's size (`SizeLimit` for the in-memory store, the server's memory limit for Redis).

## Health checks

`AddNetjes()` on the health checks builder adds a check of the Node processes:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().AddNetjes();
// ...
app.MapHealthChecks("/healthz");
```

| Status | When | `/healthz` answers |
|---|---|---|
| Healthy | Every process is ready. | 200 |
| Degraded | Some processes are restarting; the others take the renders. | 200 |
| Unhealthy | None is ready: starting, or all restarting. Documents are then [rendered in the browser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/rendering-and-streaming.md#when-no-sidecar-is-ready). | 503 |

The status codes are ASP.NET Core's defaults for `MapHealthChecks`. The template's `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml` use `/healthz` for Docker's health check.

## Telemetry

Netjes reports traces and metrics through an `ActivitySource` and a `Meter`, both named `Netjes` (`NetjesTelemetry.Name`). With OpenTelemetry:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
    .WithTracing(tracing => tracing.AddSource(NetjesTelemetry.Name).AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation())
    .WithMetrics(metrics => metrics.AddMeter(NetjesTelemetry.Name).AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation());
```

| Span | Covers | Tags |
|---|---|---|
| `netjes.loader` | A page loader | `netjes.route` |
| `netjes.action` | A page action | `netjes.route` |
| `netjes.render` | Building the payload and, for documents, rendering | `netjes.route`, `netjes.page`, `netjes.response` (`document` or `data`), `http.response.status_code` |
| `netjes.sidecar.render` | The call to a Node process (a client span) | |

The call to the Node process carries `traceparent`, and the process logs it with render errors, so its logs can be matched to the trace.

| Metric | Unit | Tags |
|---|---|---|
| `netjes.render.duration` | s | `netjes.route`, `netjes.response`, `http.response.status_code` |
| `netjes.sidecar.render.duration` | s | |
| `netjes.sidecar.fallbacks` | documents | `netjes.route` |
| `netjes.web_vitals.lcp`, `.inp`, `.fcp`, `.ttfb` | ms | `netjes.route`, `netjes.web_vitals.rating` |
| `netjes.web_vitals.cls` | | `netjes.route`, `netjes.web_vitals.rating` |

Tags carry route patterns (`/blog/[slug]`), never URLs.

### Web vitals

To collect Core Web Vitals from real visitors, turn on `NetjesOptions.CollectWebVitals`, install `web-vitals`, and render `<WebVitals />` from `netjes/vitals` in the root layout. Each page load then posts its vitals to `/_netjes/vitals`, which records them as the `netjes.web_vitals.*` histograms. The endpoint accepts anyone's reports, so it checks each one and tags it only with route patterns the app has (`unknown` otherwise). `useReportWebVitals(callback)` from the same module hands you the measurements to send elsewhere.

## Logs

Netjes logs through `ILogger`, under these categories:

| Category | What it logs |
|---|---|
| `Netjes.Sidecar.NodeSidecar` | The Node processes: their output (stdout as information, stderr as warnings, without terminal colour codes), exits with their last lines, restarts, processes taken out and back. |
| `Netjes.Sidecar.NodeSidecarHostedService` | Why the app could not start its Node processes, or in development the Vite dev server: one critical entry, after which the app exits with code 1. |
| `Netjes.Rendering.ViteManifestProvider` | That the app started in Production without a build: one critical entry, after which it exits with code 1. |
| `Netjes.Rendering.PageRenderer` | Documents sent for the browser to render, deferred values that could not be delivered, output-cached pages that cannot be stored (a nonce, an endpoint that is not keyed, the middleware order). |
| `Netjes.Rendering.PageErrorMiddleware` | Exceptions while serving a page (errors) and bad requests (warnings). |
| `Netjes.Rendering.CachePaths` | Output-cached renders that read a request cookie. |
| `Netjes.Deferred` | `Page.Defer` values that failed or could not be serialized. |
| `Netjes.ServerActions` | Server action calls that failed (errors) or were refused (warnings). |
| `Netjes.Routing.RouteDiagnostics` | [Route warnings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md) at startup. |
| `Netjes.Routing.FileSystemRouteTableProvider` | Development: route table rescans and the conflicts they find. |
| `Netjes.TypeGen.TypeGenHostedService` | Writing `generated/netjes.ts` in Development, and the `generate` and `routes` commands. |
| `Netjes.Export.StaticExportService` | `netjes export`: what it wrote, and why a page could not be exported. |

Set their levels as for any category:

```json
{
  "Logging": {
    "LogLevel": {
      "Netjes.Routing.RouteDiagnostics": "Error"
    }
  }
}
```

## Proxies and base paths

Behind a reverse proxy or a TLS-terminating load balancer, tell the app what the visitor sent, trusting only the proxy's network. The examples do it like this:

```csharp
if (app.Configuration.GetSection("ForwardedHeaders:KnownNetworks").Get<string[]>() is { Length: > 0 } proxyNetworks)
{
    var forwarded = new ForwardedHeadersOptions { ForwardedHeaders = ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto };
    forwarded.KnownIPNetworks.Clear();
    forwarded.KnownProxies.Clear();
    foreach (var network in proxyNetworks)
    {
        forwarded.KnownIPNetworks.Add(System.Net.IPNetwork.Parse(network));
    }

    app.UseForwardedHeaders(forwarded);
}

app.UseNetjes();
```

A proxy in front of a Netjes app must pass these headers through unchanged:

| Header | Direction | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Netjes-Data`, `X-Netjes-Segments` | request | Client navigations ask for the page payload, and name the layouts they hold. |
| `X-Netjes-Cookies` | response | Tells the client router that an action signed someone in or out, so it forgets the pages it keeps for Back and Forward and clears the query cache. |
| `X-Netjes-Antiforgery` | response | Marks a 400 for a refused antiforgery token, the only one the client sends again. |
| `X-Netjes-Now` | response | The server's clock, which the client uses to judge how fresh seeded data is. |

A proxy that also caches must keep responses apart by `X-Netjes-Data` and `X-Netjes-Segments` (they carry `Vary` for both), or not cache pages; see [caching](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/caching.md#cdns-and-proxies).

A proxy that rewrites `Host` makes every action fail the same-origin check until the app sees its public host. Forward the host as well (`ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedHost`, with `ForwardedHeadersOptions.AllowedHosts` set to your host names), or list the public origin in `AllowedActionOrigins`; see [security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#server-actions-and-page-actions).

To serve the app under a path, like Next.js's `basePath`, set it on both sides:

```csharp
app.UsePathBase("/docs"); // before UseNetjes()
app.UseNetjes();
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ plugins: [netjes({ basePath: '/docs' })] });
```

Links, forms, redirects and `router.push` take paths as if the app were at the root, and Netjes adds the base; see [routing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md).

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/testing.md -->

# Testing

This guide is for app developers writing tests for a Netjes app: component and page tests in Vitest with the `netjes/testing` harness, tests of C# loaders and actions with `WebApplicationFactory`, end-to-end tests in Playwright, and the checks to run in CI. An app made with `netjes new` has two component tests to start from, in `components/`.

## Vitest

The template runs Vitest with `npm test` (`vitest run`). The `netjes()` Vite plugin sets these defaults under Vitest, each only when the app's own `test` config does not set it:

- `environment: 'jsdom'`, when `jsdom` is installed;
- `exclude`: `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `bin/`, `obj/`, `e2e/` (Playwright's folder) and `.git/`;
- a setup file that unmounts what each test rendered (Testing Library's `cleanup`), when `@testing-library/react` is installed.

There is no `include` default, so Vitest finds `*.test.*` and `*.spec.*` files outside those folders. `netjes({ test: false })` adds none of them ([Vite plugin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/vite-plugin.md#vitest-defaults)).

## Component and page tests

`createTestApp()` from `netjes/testing` gives a component what a Netjes page has around it: the router, the page payload, the query client and the public config. Pass its `Wrapper` to Testing Library:

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createTestApp } from 'netjes/testing';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { Greeting } from './Greeting.tsx';

describe('Greeting', () => {
  it('links to the about page without a full page load', async () => {
    const app = createTestApp();
    render(<Greeting message="Hello" renderedAt="2026-10-28T12:00:00Z" />, { wrapper: app.Wrapper });

    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('link', { name: 'About this app' }));

    expect(app.navigations).toEqual([{ type: 'push', href: '/about' }]);
  });
});
```

The router is a fake. `<Link>`, `router.push` and `router.replace` move to the new URL, so hooks such as `usePathname()` and `useSearchParams()` see it, but no page is loaded. Every navigation, router call, form post and server action call is recorded in `app.navigations`, in order:

| Entry | For |
|---|---|
| `{ type: 'push' \| 'replace', href }` | A link, `router.push`, `router.replace` |
| `{ type: 'refresh' \| 'back' \| 'forward' }` | `router.refresh()`, `router.back()`, `router.forward()` |
| `{ type: 'submit', action, data }` | A `<Form method="post">` post, with its fields as `URLSearchParams` or `FormData` |
| `{ type: 'action', name, input }` | A server action call, with its input (an object, or the form's `FormData`) |

### Options

| Option | What it sets |
|---|---|
| `url` | The current URL. Default `/`. |
| `route` | The page's route pattern, such as `/blog/[slug]`. |
| `params` | What `useParams()` returns. |
| `shared` | The shared props, as the server would send them. |
| `queries` | Entries seeded into the query client, as `.WithQuery` seeds them: `[{ key, data }]`. |
| `defaultOptions` | TanStack Query defaults, like `netjes({ query: { defaultOptions } })`. Retries are off. |
| `queryClient` | A client of your own instead. |
| `actions` | Answers for server action calls, by name (below). |
| `navigation` | What `useNavigation()` returns. Default idle. |
| `antiforgery` | The token `<Form method="post">` adds. Default a test token; `false` for none. |
| `publicConfig` | What `usePublicConfig()` returns. |
| `locale` | What `useLocale()` returns. |
| `draftMode` | What `useDraftMode()` reports. |

`createTestApp()` returns `{ Wrapper, navigations, queryClient }`. The [React API reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/react-api.md#createtestapp) has the types.

### Answering server actions

`actions` answers calls by name, as the C# action would. An action without an answer succeeds with no result. A failure can name the fields its state's `values` keep, as the server does for the fields an action declares:

```tsx
const app = createTestApp({
  actions: {
    'home.greet': () => ({ ok: false, status: 422, errors: { name: ['Tell us your name.'] }, fields: ['name'] }),
  },
});
render(<HelloForm />, { wrapper: app.Wrapper });

await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Say hello' }));

expect(await screen.findByText('Tell us your name.')).toBeDefined();
```

An answer can also carry `queries` (`[{ key, data }]`) and `invalidate` (query keys), like `.WithQuery` and `.Invalidate` on a C# result.

The `Wrapper` puts its stand-in for the router in place before the components inside it run any effect, so an action a component calls from `useEffect` or `useLayoutEffect` as it mounts is answered and recorded like any other call. Render such a component inside the `Wrapper`: outside it there is no router to wait for, and the call fails at once with "called before the page was ready".

### Pages

A page file's default export is a component like any other. Render it with the props its loader would send; `definePage` checks them against the generated schema, as it does in the app, so a test with props the schema rejects fails the way the page would:

```tsx
import Guestbook from './page.tsx';

it('shows the validation errors the action sent back, next to their fields', () => {
  const app = createTestApp({ url: '/guestbook' });

  render(<Guestbook entries={[]} errors={{ name: 'Tell us your name.' }} values={{ name: '', message: 'Hi' }} />, {
    wrapper: app.Wrapper,
  });

  expect(screen.getByText('Tell us your name.')).toBeDefined();
});
```

A component that fetches its own data with `useQuery` gets seeded data from `queries`. For what it fetches after that, answer the requests with a mock server such as [MSW](https://mswjs.io), as the Blog example's `LikeButton.test.tsx` does.

## C# tests of loaders and actions

### Loaders as plain methods

`Page.Props(x)` returns a `PageResult<T>` whose `Props` holds `x` (null for a redirect or not-found), so you can call a loader written as a method from a test:

```csharp
public static class HomePage
{
    public sealed record HomeProps(string Message, DateTimeOffset RenderedAt);

    public static PageResult<HomeProps> Home(TimeProvider time) => Page.Props(new HomeProps("Hello from C#", time.GetUtcNow()));

    public static void MapHomePage(this IEndpointRouteBuilder app) => app.MapPageLoader("/", Home);
}

[Fact]
public void Home_SaysHello() => Assert.Equal("Hello from C#", HomePage.Home(TimeProvider.System).Props?.Message);
```

### The app over HTTP

`WebApplicationFactory` from `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing` runs the real app in memory, with its pipeline, authorization and services. Two settings let it run without a client build or Node: development mode, so the routes come from the files in `app/`, and a stand-in for the renderer, so no sidecar starts. The TaskBoard example's tests do this:

```csharp
public sealed class AppFactory : WebApplicationFactory<Program>
{
    public FakeRenderer Renderer { get; } = new();

    protected override void ConfigureWebHost(IWebHostBuilder builder)
    {
        builder.UseEnvironment("Testing");
        // Development mode reads the routes from app/ on disk; nothing is rendered, so no Vite or Node is needed.
        builder.UseSetting("Netjes:Mode", "Development");
        builder.ConfigureServices(services => services.AddSingleton<ISsrRenderer>(Renderer));
    }
}

/// <summary>Keeps the payload of the last document instead of rendering it.</summary>
public sealed class FakeRenderer : ISsrRenderer
{
    public string? Last { get; private set; }

    public Task<string> RenderAsync(string payloadJson, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        Last = payloadJson;
        return Task.FromResult("<!DOCTYPE html><html><body>rendered</body></html>");
    }
}
```

The test project references the app's project and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing`; ASP.NET Core 10 makes the `Program` class of top-level statements public, so `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` can start it. In development mode the app also writes `generated/netjes.ts` at startup when it is out of date, as `dotnet run` does.

When the app cannot start, `CreateClient()` throws why, as an `InvalidOperationException` whose message says what to do: `No production build found at …` for a test that runs the app in Production without a build, or `Could not start 'node'. …` for one that renders with the real Node processes where Node.js is not installed. Run as its own program, the app logs that message in one line and exits with code 1 instead ([deployment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/deployment.md#what-the-server-needs)).

A host that the test project builds itself with `WebApplication.CreateBuilder`, rather than `WebApplicationFactory`, has the test assembly's name, so Netjes takes it for the program: when its Node processes cannot start, `StartAsync()` returns, and the app logs why and stops. Give it another name with `WebApplicationOptions.ApplicationName`, as `WebApplicationFactory` gives the app its own, and `StartAsync()` throws instead.

Talk to it as the client router does. A request with `X-Netjes-Data: 1` gets the page payload as JSON:

```csharp
public sealed class HomePageTests(AppFactory app) : IClassFixture<AppFactory>
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task TheHomePage_HasTheLoadersMessage()
    {
        var client = app.CreateClient();
        var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "/");
        request.Headers.Add(NetjesHeaders.Data, "1");

        var response = await client.SendAsync(request, TestContext.Current.CancellationToken);
        var payload = JsonNode.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(TestContext.Current.CancellationToken))!;

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.OK, response.StatusCode);
        Assert.Equal("Hello from C#", (string?)payload["props"]!["message"]);
    }
}
```

A page with `Page.Defer` values answers with NDJSON: the payload on the first line, then one line per value. A document request (without the header) goes through the fake renderer, whose `Last` then holds the payload the sidecar would have rendered.

A server action needs an antiforgery token. Get one from `/_netjes/antiforgery`, which also sets the antiforgery cookie (the factory's client keeps cookies), and send it as the header the response names:

```csharp
[Fact]
public async Task Greeting_WithoutAName_IsAFieldError()
{
    var client = app.CreateClient();
    var token = JsonNode.Parse(await client.GetStringAsync("/_netjes/antiforgery", TestContext.Current.CancellationToken))!;
    var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "/_netjes/actions/home.greet")
    {
        Content = new FormUrlEncodedContent([new("name", "")]),
    };
    request.Headers.Add(NetjesHeaders.Data, "1");
    request.Headers.Add((string)token["headerName"]!, (string)token["requestToken"]!);

    var response = await client.SendAsync(request, TestContext.Current.CancellationToken);
    var result = JsonNode.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(TestContext.Current.CancellationToken))!;

    Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.UnprocessableEntity, response.StatusCode);
    Assert.Equal("Tell us your name.", (string?)result["errors"]!["name"]![0]);
}
```

Without `X-Netjes-Data` the same post is a form post without JavaScript: put the token in the form field `token["formFieldName"]` instead, and expect a 303 redirect on success, or the form's page rendered again with status 422.

`tests/TaskBoard.Tests` has a fuller harness: a `Browser` type that keeps cookies and the last token, signs up users and calls actions, against Postgres in Testcontainers.

## End-to-end tests

Playwright tests the app in a real browser. The examples run each suite against two servers at once, one in Development (the Vite dev server) and one in Production (the build), since some failures show in one only. A server in the Playwright config waits for the app's health check:

```ts
webServer: [
  {
    command: 'dotnet run --no-build --no-launch-profile',
    url: `${DEV_URL}/healthz`,
    env: { ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: 'Development', ASPNETCORE_URLS: DEV_URL, Netjes__ViteDevPort: VITE_PORT },
    reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
  },
  {
    command: 'npm run build && dotnet run --no-build --no-launch-profile',
    url: `${PROD_URL}/healthz`,
    env: { ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: 'Production', ASPNETCORE_URLS: PROD_URL },
    reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
  },
],
```

`--no-build` starts the last build, so build the app first: the examples' `test:e2e` script is `dotnet build && playwright test`. Give each development server its own `Netjes__ViteDevPort`, so two of them can run side by side. Put the specs in `e2e/`, which the Vitest defaults leave out, and install the browser once with `npx playwright install chromium`. `examples/Blog/playwright.config.ts` also runs the app under a base path, with no Node process ready (the client-rendered fallback), and as a static export.

## In CI

```bash
npm ci
npx netjes generate --check            # the committed generated/netjes.ts matches the C# code
npm run typecheck
npm test                               # Vitest
dotnet test -c Release                 # loaders and actions
dotnet build                           # the Debug build that dotnet run --no-build starts
npx playwright install --with-deps chromium && npx playwright test
```

`netjes generate --check` runs the app once in command mode, without a build or a Node process and on a throwaway loopback port, and exits 1 when the generated types are out of date. An app that does not start, such as one with a loader or action minimal APIs cannot bind, fails the check with the exception's message. Startup code that needs a database can skip that work with `app.GetNetjesCommand()`; see the [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/cli.md#netjes-generate).

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/redirects-rewrites-headers.md -->

# Redirects, rewrites and headers

This guide is for app developers looking for what Next.js configures in `next.config.js`: `redirects`, `rewrites`, `headers`, `basePath` and `i18n`. In Netjes these are ASP.NET Core features, configured in `Program.cs` (or `appsettings.json`), next to authentication and the rest of the pipeline.

## Redirects

Next.js's `redirects()` is the URL Rewriting middleware, placed before `UseNetjes()`:

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Rewrite;

app.UseRewriter(new RewriteOptions()
    .AddRedirect("^old-blog/(.*)", "blog/$1", statusCode: StatusCodes.Status308PermanentRedirect)
    .AddRedirectToHttpsPermanent());
app.UseNetjes();
```

For redirects that depend on data (a renamed slug), return `Page.Redirect(...)` from the page's loader instead. It works for document requests and client navigations alike: the client router follows it without a full page load. See [security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#redirects) for the URLs it accepts, and `Page.LocalRedirect` for URLs that come from the request.

## Rewrites

Internal rewrites, where the URL stays and another page answers (Next.js's `rewrites()`), are the rewriter too:

```csharp
app.UseRewriter(new RewriteOptions().AddRewrite("^docs/latest/(.*)", "docs/v2/$1", skipRemainingRules: true));
```

Rewrites to another host (an external `destination` in Next.js) are a reverse proxy, such as [YARP](https://microsoft.github.io/reverse-proxy/) (MIT), mapped next to the pages:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddReverseProxy().LoadFromConfig(builder.Configuration.GetSection("ReverseProxy"));
// ...
app.MapReverseProxy(); // e.g. /api/legacy/{**rest} → https://legacy.example.com
```

## Headers

Netjes already sends `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` and `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` with every document (see [security headers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#security-headers)), leaving out any the app has set itself. An app that sends its own `X-Frame-Options`, as below, or a policy with `frame-ancestors`, decides about framing alone: Netjes then adds neither framing header.

Set headers for all pages with a small middleware, or for some pages with an endpoint filter, where Next.js has `headers()`:

```csharp
app.Use((http, next) =>
{
    http.Response.Headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY";
    http.Response.Headers["Permissions-Policy"] = "camera=(), microphone=()";
    return next(http);
});

app.MapPages().AddEndpointFilter(async (context, next) =>
{
    context.HttpContext.Response.Headers["X-Robots-Tag"] = "noindex";
    return await next(context);
});
```

For a Content-Security-Policy, use `NetjesOptions.ContentSecurityPolicy` rather than a header of your own, so the nonce Netjes puts on its scripts matches the header, or call `HttpContext.GetCspNonce()` when you write the policy yourself. A policy with `{nonce}` keeps pages out of the output cache; a hash-based one lets them be cached, but its pages must not stream. [Security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md#content-security-policy) explains both, and [static export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/static-export.md#deferred-values-and-suspense) what a static host's policy does to exported pages. NetEscapades.AspNetCore.SecurityHeaders (MIT) covers the other headers declaratively.

## Base path

Next.js's `basePath` is `UsePathBase` in .NET and the `basePath` option of the Vite plugin, set to the same value:

```csharp
app.UsePathBase("/docs"); // before UseNetjes()
```

```ts
netjes({ basePath: '/docs' }) // vite.config.ts: built asset URLs get the prefix
```

Write links, form actions, redirects and `router.push` paths as if the app were at the root; Netjes adds the base. `usePathname()` leaves it out. For a raw URL such as `<link rel="icon">`, prefix it yourself with `useBasePath()`, or build it with `useHref(path)`, as with Next.js. [Base path](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#base-path) in the routing guide has the rules.

## Internationalized routing

Next.js's `i18n` routing is a `[lang]` folder with Netjes's locale routing turned on ([Locales](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#locales) in the routing guide):

```csharp
builder.Services.AddNetjesLocalization(o => o.SupportedCultures = ["en", "nl"]); // the first is the default
builder.Services.AddLocalization();
// ...
app.UseNetjes();
app.UseNetjesLocalization(); // after UseNetjes: it reads the [lang] route value
app.MapLocaleRedirect();     // "/" → "/nl" for a Dutch browser
```

Loaders run with `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture` set, so formatting and `IStringLocalizer<T>` follow the URL.

- Only the URL decides. Pages outside `[lang]` get the default culture, not one from a cookie or `Accept-Language`, because an output-cached copy would otherwise serve the first visitor's language to everyone. If such pages are not cached and should follow the browser, add `AcceptLanguageHeaderRequestCultureProvider` to `RequestLocalizationOptions.RequestCultureProviders` yourself (and vary any caching by `Accept-Language`).
- Netjes turns off parent-culture fallback, so a name matches only a configured culture exactly: list `nl-BE` as well as `nl` if both should match. The `/` redirect from `MapLocaleRedirect` is separate: it sends an `nl-BE` browser to `/nl`.
- An unsupported locale renders the 404 page in the default culture. Any other endpoint whose route has the locale parameter (a minimal API at `/{lang}/api/...`) answers a bare 404 for one too, so give a parameter that is not a locale another name.
- A supported locale in another case (`/EN/about`) reaches loaders and `params.lang` as configured (`en`).
- The route parameter is `lang` unless you set `NetjesLocalizationOptions.RouteParameter`.

The document's `<html lang>` follows the locale, and `useLocale()` returns it in React. Send the page's strings through shared props:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddNetjes(options => options.UseSharedProps(http =>
{
    var strings = http.RequestServices.GetRequiredService<IStringLocalizer<SharedResource>>();
    return ValueTask.FromResult(new SiteStrings(strings.GetAllStrings().ToDictionary(s => s.Name, s => s.Value)));
}));

public sealed record SiteStrings(Dictionary<string, string> Messages);
```

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/coding-agents.md -->

# Coding agents

Netjes gives coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and the like) three things: the docs as plain text, a guide in each app, and a skill with the conventions in short.

## The docs as text

- [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/llms.txt) is an index of the docs in the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format: a summary, then a link and a line for each document, the `netjes` skill below included, so an agent can read it in an app that does not have it.
- [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/llms-full.txt) has those documents in one file, for agents that take a whole file as context. It leaves out the ones `llms.txt` marks as not in it: the architecture page, the benchmarks and the example apps' READMEs, which an agent building an app does not need.

Both follow the `main` branch, so they can describe a newer version than the one an app uses. The installed version's sources and types are in the app's `node_modules/netjes/`.

## A new app

`npx netjes new my-app` writes, next to the code:

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | Any agent that reads `AGENTS.md`: how the app is laid out (`app/`, `Features/`, `generated/netjes.ts`), the commands, how to add a page with data, the rules (C# decides, zod at the boundaries, TanStack Query for server state, never edit generated files) and the checks to run before finishing. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code, which reads `CLAUDE.md`: one line, `@AGENTS.md`, which imports the guide. |
| `.claude/skills/netjes/` | The `netjes` skill ([SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/SKILL.md)) and references for routing, data and actions, caching and streaming, testing and deployment. Claude Code loads skills from `.claude/skills/`; `AGENTS.md` points other agents at the folder. |

Commit them with the app. `AGENTS.md` is the app's own from then on: add the rules of your codebase to it.

## An existing app

[`netjes agents`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/cli.md#netjes-agents) adds them. Run it in the app's directory (the one with the `.csproj`), or with that directory as the argument:

```bash
npx netjes agents            # or: npx netjes agents path/to/app
```

It writes the same three, with the project file's name as the title of `AGENTS.md` (`--name` sets another; without a single `.csproj` it takes the directory's name and warns on stderr that it did, so run it in the right folder or pass `--name`). It never replaces a file that exists: it prints the directory, then each file it wrote or kept, and if a `CLAUDE.md` of your own does not import `AGENTS.md`, it says to add the line `@AGENTS.md`. `--force` replaces them all.

## After upgrading Netjes

The skill and `AGENTS.md` describe the version that wrote them. The skill belongs to Netjes, so replace it with the installed version's:

```bash
rm -r .claude/skills/netjes && npx netjes agents
```

That keeps `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, which belong to the app. To compare your `AGENTS.md` with the installed version's, run `npx netjes agents --force`, which replaces all three, and use `git diff` to keep your own additions.

## Working on Netjes itself

The repository has its own [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/AGENTS.md) (which `CLAUDE.md` imports), for people and agents changing Netjes, and the skills [netjes-contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/.claude/skills/netjes-contributing/SKILL.md) (making a change, from branch to merge) and [netjes-verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/.claude/skills/netjes-verification/SKILL.md) (proving it works) in `.claude/skills/`. `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` are generated from the docs by `scripts/llms.mjs`: run `npm run docs:llms` after changing a document, and `npm run docs:check` fails while they are out of date or while a link in the docs points at nothing. In a git checkout they are built only from the documents git tracks, so `git add` a new one first.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/react-api.md -->

# React API

This is the reference for the npm package `netjes`: every export of every entry point, with its signature and what it does, for app developers looking up an API. The guides explain how the pieces fit: [Routing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md), [Data loading](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md), [Actions and forms](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md), [Metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/metadata.md), [Images](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/images.md) and [Testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/testing.md). The C# side is in the [C# API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/csharp-api.md).

## Entry points

| Import | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [`netjes`](#netjes) | Components, hooks and functions for pages: links, forms, server actions, images, scripts, metadata types |
| [`netjes/zod`](#netjeszod) | `deferred()`, the zod schema for `Page.Defer` values |
| [`netjes/testing`](#netjestesting) | `createTestApp()`, the harness for component and page tests |
| [`netjes/testing/setup`](#netjestestingsetup) | A Vitest setup file that unmounts what each test rendered |
| [`netjes/vitals`](#netjesvitals) | Core Web Vitals: `useReportWebVitals()` and `<WebVitals />` |
| [`netjes/vite`](#netjesvite) | The `netjes()` Vite plugin |
| [`netjes/client-entry`, `netjes/server-entry`, `netjes/sidecar`](#internal-entry-points) | Used by the plugin and the .NET app, not by app code |

The package also has the `netjes` command ([the netjes command](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/cli.md)). The app's own `generated/netjes.ts` is described under [The generated module](#the-generated-module).

## `netjes`

### Pages and layouts

#### `definePage`

```ts
function definePage<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1>(
  schema: Schema,
  Page: ComponentType<StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<Schema>>,
): FunctionComponent<Record<string, unknown>>;
```

Declares a page whose props, sent by its C# loader, are validated before it renders. The component gets the parsed, typed props. Props the schema rejects throw `Invalid props: <issues>` to the nearest error boundary. Use the generated schema: `export default definePage(pages['/blog/[slug]'], function Post({ post }) { ... })`. Any [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) works (zod, valibot, arktype), as long as it validates synchronously.

#### `defineLayout`

```ts
function defineLayout<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1>(
  schema: Schema,
  Layout: ComponentType<StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<Schema> & LayoutProps>,
): FunctionComponent<LayoutProps & Record<string, unknown>>;
```

The same for a layout with a C# layout loader (`MapLayoutLoader`): its props are validated (`Invalid layout props: ...`) and the component gets them next to `children` and `params`. Use the generated schema: `defineLayout(layouts['app/docs'], function DocsLayout({ toc, children }) { ... })`.

#### `LayoutProps`

```ts
type LayoutProps = { children: ReactNode; params: Params };
```

The props of every layout component. A layout with parallel routes also gets each slot as a prop named after its folder ([Parallel routes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#parallel-routes)).

#### `ErrorPageProps`

```ts
type ErrorPageProps = { error: Error & { status?: number }; reset: () => void };
```

The props of an `error.tsx`: what was thrown, with the HTTP status when the server rendered the page for an error, and `reset()` to render the segment again.

### Navigation

#### `Link`

```ts
function Link(props: LinkProps): JSX.Element;

type LinkProps = Omit<AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement>, 'href'> & {
  href: Href;
  replace?: boolean;            // replace the history entry instead of adding one
  scroll?: boolean;             // default true: scroll to the top, or to the #fragment
  prefetch?: 'intent' | 'none'; // default 'intent': fetch the page on hover, focus and touch
  reloadDocument?: boolean;     // let the browser load the URL with a full page load
};
```

An `<a>` that navigates on the client. It sets `aria-current="page"` when its path is the current one, and puts its `href` under the base path. Modified clicks, other mouse buttons, a `target` other than `_self`, `download` and URLs on another origin behave like a plain link. See [Links](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#links).

#### `useRouter`

```ts
function useRouter(): Router;

type Router = {
  push(href: Href, options?: { scroll?: boolean }): Promise<void>;
  replace(href: Href, options?: { scroll?: boolean }): Promise<void>;
  prefetch(href: Href): void;
  refresh(): Promise<void>;
  back(): void;
  forward(): void;
};
```

The client router. `push` and `replace` navigate, adding or replacing a history entry. `prefetch` loads a page ahead, as a link does on hover. `refresh` loads the page on screen from the server again in place: every loader runs, in the same history entry, with the URL's fragment, without scrolling. `back` and `forward` go through history, showing remembered pages without a request. Throws outside a Netjes page.

#### `useNavigation`

```ts
function useNavigation(): NavigationState;

type NavigationState =
  | { state: 'idle'; error?: SubmitError }
  | { state: 'loading' | 'submitting'; location: string };

type SubmitError = { status: number | null; action: string };
```

The router's state: `'loading'` during a navigation and `'submitting'` during a form post, with the path and query on their way (without the base path). After a form post that did not produce a page, `'idle'` carries `error` until the next navigation: the status of the error response, or `null` when nothing answered, and the URL posted to.

#### `usePathname`

```ts
function usePathname(): string;
```

The current path, without the base path: `/blog/hello`.

#### `useSearchParams`

```ts
function useSearchParams(): URLSearchParams;
function useSearchParams<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1>(schema: Schema): StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<Schema>;
```

The query string. With a schema, it parses an object of the values (a string each, or an array of strings for a key that repeats) and drops the values the schema rejects, so its defaults and optional fields apply; only a value that stays invalid without them throws. Define the schema at module level.

#### `useParams`

```ts
function useParams(): Params;
function useParams<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1>(schema: Schema): StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<Schema>;
```

The page's route values, catch-all values as arrays (empty for an optional catch-all). A single parameter the request has no value for is `null`, as when a page is rendered with `Page.Render` from an endpoint whose route lacks it. With a schema, parsed by it; a rejected value throws `Invalid route params: ...` to the error boundary, so constrain route values in C#. Define the schema at module level.

#### `useSelectedLayoutSegment`

```ts
function useSelectedLayoutSegment(): string | null;
```

In a layout: the URL segment one level below it, decoded, such as the active tab; `null` at the layout's own page.

#### `useSelectedLayoutSegments`

```ts
function useSelectedLayoutSegments(): string[];
```

In a layout: every URL segment below it, decoded. Route groups do not appear, since they are not in the URL. Outside a layout, the whole path.

#### `useBasePath`

```ts
function useBasePath(): string;
```

The base path the app is mounted under with `UsePathBase`, or `''` at the root. For URLs in your own markup that Netjes does not prefix, such as `<link rel="icon" href={`${basePath}/favicon.svg`}>`.

#### `useHref`

```ts
function useHref(href: string): string;
```

`href` under the base path, for a plain `<a href>` or another attribute: what `<Link>` does for its own. Root-relative paths get the base path unless they already start with it; other URLs are returned as they are.

#### `useLocale`

```ts
function useLocale(): string | null;
```

The request culture the page was rendered in with `AddNetjesLocalization`, such as `'nl'`; `null` without localization. See [Locales](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/routing.md#locales).

### Forms and server actions

#### `Form`

```ts
function Form(props: FormProps): JSX.Element;

type FormProps = Omit<FormHTMLAttributes<HTMLFormElement>, 'method' | 'action'> & {
  method?: 'get' | 'post';        // default 'get'
  action?: string | FormAction;   // default: the current URL
  replace?: boolean;              // for a GET form: replace the history entry
  reloadDocument?: boolean;       // let the browser submit it, with a full page load
};

type FormAction = (formData: FormData) => void | Promise<void>;
```

A `<form>` that submits without a full page load and treats the answer like a navigation. A GET form navigates to its action with the fields as the query string. A POST form posts with `fetch`, adds the antiforgery token, follows a redirect or shows the page the server rendered, and leaves a response that is not a page as it is (an HTML document is shown, an attachment downloaded, a failure reported through `useNavigation()`). With a function `action`, React runs it, so `useFormStatus` works; for `useAction`'s `formAction` the server renders a real post to the action, so the form works without JavaScript too. See [`<Form>` in detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md#form-in-detail).

#### `SubmitButton`

```ts
function SubmitButton(props: SubmitButtonProps): JSX.Element;

type SubmitButtonProps = Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, 'type'>;
```

A submit button whose `formAction` is rendered under the base path, so it posts to the right place with and without JavaScript.

#### `serverAction`

```ts
function serverAction<TInput = FormData, TResult = unknown>(
  name: string,
  options?: { result?: StandardSchemaV1<unknown, TResult> },
): ServerAction<TInput, TResult>;

interface ServerAction<TInput, TResult> {
  (input: TInput | FormData): Promise<ActionState<TResult>>;
  readonly actionName: string;
  readonly url: string; // /_netjes/actions/{name}
}
```

A reference to a C# server action (`app.MapAction(name, ...)`). Call it with a plain object, sent as JSON, or with `FormData`, sent as a form post; pass it to `useAction` for a form. With `options.result`, the result is parsed by that schema. A 422 resolves to `{ ok: false, ... }`; any other failure throws a `ServerActionError`. A call made as the page starts waits up to 10 seconds for the router; with no router on its way, as on the server or in a test outside `createTestApp`'s `Wrapper`, it throws at once ([calls as the page starts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md#calls-as-the-page-starts)). The generated `serverActions` map holds a typed reference, made with this function, for every action.

#### `useAction`

```ts
function useAction<TInput, TResult>(
  action: ServerAction<TInput, TResult>,
  options?: UseActionOptions<TResult>,
): [state: ActionState<TResult> | null, formAction: (formData: FormData) => void, isPending: boolean];

type UseActionOptions<TResult> = {
  initialState?: ActionState<TResult> | null; // default null
  onSubmit?: (formData: FormData) => void;    // runs inside the action's transition, before the call
};
```

React's `useActionState` for a server action. Pass `formAction` to `<Form action>`. After a failed post without JavaScript, `state` starts as that failure, with the submitted values. `onSubmit` is where `useOptimistic` updates go: React keeps them until the action and the page refresh after it have finished. See [`useAction` and `<Form>`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md#useaction-and-form).

#### `ActionState`

```ts
type ActionState<TResult> =
  | { ok: true; result: TResult }
  | { ok: false; status: number; errors: Record<string, string[]>; values?: Record<string, string | string[]> };
```

The value a server action call resolves to: its result, or the validation errors per field (status 422) and, for a form, the submitted values of the fields the action declares. An action that answers `ServerAction.Redirect(...)` or `Ok()` resolves with `result` undefined, whatever its type says.

#### `usePageActionState`

```ts
function usePageActionState(): PageActionFailure | null;

type PageActionFailure = { ok: false; status: number; errors: Record<string, string[]>; values: Record<string, string | string[]> };
```

After the input of the page's action (`MapPageAction`) failed its DataAnnotations or `IValidatableObject` checks: the errors per field (status 422) and the submitted values of the fields the action declares, in the shape of `ActionState`'s failure. The page has been rendered again from its loader, with or without JavaScript, so a field takes its value with `defaultValue={String(failed?.values.name ?? '')}`. Null on every other render, also after a server action's failure, which `useAction` reads. See [validation in page actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md#validation-in-page-actions).

#### `ServerActionError`

```ts
class ServerActionError extends Error {
  name: 'ServerActionError';
  readonly status: number;
}
```

Thrown by a server action call when the server could not run the action or refused it (403, 404, 413, 429, 500, a refused token), as opposed to validation errors. Uncaught in a transition or an action, it reaches the nearest error boundary. Catch it to handle a status on the form, as TaskBoard does for 429.

### Server data

#### `useSharedProps`

```ts
function useSharedProps(): unknown;
function useSharedProps<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1>(schema: Schema): StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<Schema>;
```

The props every page and layout gets from `options.UseSharedProps(...)` in C#. Pass the generated `sharedProps` schema to get them parsed and typed (`Invalid shared props: ...` when they do not match); without a schema they are `unknown`.

#### `usePublicConfig`

```ts
function usePublicConfig(): unknown;
function usePublicConfig<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1>(schema: Schema): StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<Schema>;
```

The `Netjes:PublicConfig` configuration section, sent with the first document: keys camelCased, values strings. Parse it with a coercing schema (`z.coerce.number()`, `z.stringbool()`); a mismatch throws `Invalid public config: ...`. See [Public configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md#public-configuration).

#### `useDraftMode`

```ts
function useDraftMode(): { isEnabled: boolean };
```

Whether the page was rendered in draft mode (`IDraftMode.Enable()` in C#), like Next.js's `draftMode()`. See [Caching](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/caching.md).

#### `useNonce`

```ts
function useNonce(): string | undefined;
```

The page's Content-Security-Policy nonce, for inline scripts and styles of your own; `undefined` without a policy, or under one without `{nonce}`. `<Script>` uses it by itself. See [Security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/security.md).

### Components

#### `Image`

```ts
function Image(props: ImageProps): JSX.Element;

type ImageProps = Omit<ImgHTMLAttributes<HTMLImageElement>, 'src' | 'srcSet' | 'width' | 'height' | 'loading' | 'alt'> & {
  src: string;           // a path in public/ or a URL on an allowed remote host
  alt: string;           // '' for a decorative image
  width: number;         // the intrinsic size in CSS pixels
  height: number;
  sizes?: string;        // for a responsive image: every configured width becomes a candidate
  quality?: number;      // 1-100, default 75, rounded to the nearest accepted quality
  priority?: boolean;    // load eagerly with high priority, and preload from the head
  unoptimized?: boolean; // serve src as it is
};
```

An `<img>` that reserves its space, loads lazily and offers resized copies from `/_netjes/image`: a 1x and a 2x copy for a fixed size, every configured width with `sizes`. SVGs, `data:` and `blob:` URLs are used as they are. See [Images](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/images.md).

#### `Script`

```ts
function Script(props: ScriptProps): null;

type ScriptProps = Omit<ScriptHTMLAttributes<HTMLScriptElement>, 'onLoad' | 'onError' | 'children' | 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML'> & {
  id?: string;                       // required for an inline script
  strategy?: ScriptStrategy;         // default 'afterInteractive'
  onLoad?: (event: Event) => void;
  onError?: (event: Event) => void;
  children?: string;                 // inline code, instead of src
};

type ScriptStrategy = 'beforeInteractive' | 'afterInteractive' | 'lazyOnload';
```

A third-party script that does not block the page, like `next/script`. Each is added to the document once, by `id` or `src`. `afterInteractive` adds it after hydration, `lazyOnload` once the page has loaded and the browser is idle, and `beforeInteractive` writes an external script into the server-rendered head. The page's CSP nonce is added when there is one. See [Third-party scripts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/metadata.md#third-party-scripts-script).

#### `dynamic`

```ts
function dynamic<P extends object>(
  load: () => Promise<{ default: ComponentType<P> } | ComponentType<P>>,
  options?: DynamicOptions,
): ComponentType<P>;

type DynamicOptions = {
  ssr?: boolean;           // default true; false renders `loading` on the server and while hydrating
  loading?: ComponentType; // shown while the module loads
};
```

Like `next/dynamic`: a component whose module loads on demand, in its own chunk, inside a Suspense boundary. `dynamic(() => import('./Chart.tsx'), { loading: Spinner })`. With `ssr: false` it renders only in the browser, for code that needs `window`. See [Rendering and streaming](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/rendering-and-streaming.md).

#### `clientOnly`

```ts
function clientOnly<P extends object>(Component: ComponentType<P>, options?: { fallback?: ReactNode }): ComponentType<P>;
```

A component that renders only in the browser, after hydration; `fallback` (default nothing) on the server and until then. The switch is hydration-safe.

### Metadata types

#### `Metadata`

```ts
type Metadata = {
  title?: MetadataTitle;
  description?: string;
  keywords?: string[];
  authors?: { name: string; url?: string }[];
  robots?: string | { index?: boolean; follow?: boolean };
  alternates?: { canonical?: string; languages?: Record<string, string> };
  openGraph?: {
    title?: string; description?: string; url?: string; siteName?: string; type?: string; locale?: string;
    images?: string | URL | MetadataImage | (string | URL | MetadataImage)[];
  };
  twitter?: {
    card?: 'summary' | 'summary_large_image' | 'app' | 'player';
    site?: string; creator?: string; title?: string; description?: string;
    images?: string | URL | MetadataImage | (string | URL | MetadataImage)[];
  };
  icons?: { icon?: string; apple?: string };
  themeColor?: string;
  other?: Record<string, string>;
};
```

The type of `export const metadata` in pages, layouts and special pages. See [Metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/metadata.md) for how it is merged and which tags it writes.

#### `MetadataTitle`

```ts
type MetadataTitle = string | { default?: string; template?: string; absolute?: string };
```

A title, or a layout's default and template (`'%s · Site'`), or an absolute title that skips templates.

#### `MetadataImage`

```ts
type MetadataImage = { url: string | URL; width?: number; height?: number; alt?: string };
```

An image for `openGraph.images` or `twitter.images`, which also take a plain URL (a string or a `URL`), and one image or an array of them. `url` is written as `og:image` or `twitter:image`; `width`, `height` and `alt` follow it as `og:image:width`, `og:image:height` and `og:image:alt`, when given; an empty `alt` or a zero `width` or `height` writes no tag. A Twitter image writes only `twitter:image:alt` besides its URL.

### Routes and hrefs

#### `Href`

```ts
type Href = Register extends { href: infer H extends string } ? H : string;
```

The type of the URLs `<Link href>` and the router accept: the app's routes once the generated file has registered them, any string before that. The generated file has an `Href` type and schema of its own for the same set.

#### `Register`

```ts
interface Register {}
```

Filled in by the generated file through declaration merging, which types `Href`: `declare module 'netjes' { interface Register { href: Href } }`.

#### `buildHref`

```ts
function buildHref(pattern: string, params: Record<string, unknown>, search?: SearchParamsInput): string;
```

The URL of a route pattern written in file syntax (`/blog/[slug]`, `/docs/[...path]`, `/shop/[[...filters]]`), with every segment value encoded and catch-all values taken as arrays. A missing or empty required value throws `netjes: route '<pattern>' needs the parameter '<name>'`. The generated `route()` calls it with typed parameters.

#### `SearchParamsInput`

```ts
type SearchParamsInput = Record<string, SearchValue | readonly SearchValue[]>;
```

The query of `buildHref` and `route()`. An array repeats the key; `null` and `undefined` are left out.

#### `SearchValue`

```ts
type SearchValue = string | number | boolean | null | undefined;
```

One query value.

#### `isRouteHref`

```ts
function isRouteHref(value: string, patterns: readonly string[]): boolean;
```

Whether a URL is one of the app's pages (by route pattern), a link within the page (`?…`, `#…`), or an `http(s):`, `mailto:` or `tel:` URL. `//host` and `/\host` are not. The generated `isHref()` and `Href` schema call it.

### Payload types

#### `Params`

```ts
type Params = Record<string, string | string[] | null>;
```

Route values: a string per single segment, an array per catch-all.

#### `PageKind`

```ts
type PageKind = 'notFound' | 'error' | 'forbidden' | 'unauthorized';
```

The reason the server rendered a boundary file instead of the route's page.

#### `SegmentRef`

```ts
type SegmentRef = {
  id: string;                  // the folder, e.g. app/blog
  layout?: string; template?: string; loading?: string; error?: string;
  props?: Record<string, unknown>;      // from the layout loader
  key?: string;                // identifies what the layout loader saw
  reused?: boolean;            // the loader was skipped; the client keeps its props
  slots?: Record<string, string | null>;
  depth?: number;
  slotParams?: Record<string, Params>;
};
```

A folder's segment files in the page payload, outermost first. Useful when inspecting payloads in tests.

#### `SeededQuery`

```ts
type SeededQuery = { key: readonly unknown[]; data: unknown; updatedAt: number };
```

A TanStack Query entry seeded by `.WithQuery(key, data)` in C#; `updatedAt` is in Unix milliseconds, on the server's clock.

#### `StandardSchemaV1`

```ts
interface StandardSchemaV1<Input = unknown, Output = Input> {
  readonly '~standard': {
    readonly version: 1;
    readonly vendor: string;
    readonly validate: (value: unknown) => StandardSchemaV1.Result<Output> | Promise<StandardSchemaV1.Result<Output>>;
    readonly types?: { readonly input: Input; readonly output: Output };
  };
}
```

The [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) interface that zod, valibot, arktype and others implement, which every schema-taking API here accepts. Netjes validates synchronously: an async schema throws.

## `netjes/zod`

The only module that imports zod, so an app on another schema library does not need it.

#### `deferred`

```ts
function deferred<Schema extends z.ZodType>(schema: Schema): z.ZodType<PromiseLike<z.output<Schema>>, Promise<unknown>>;
```

The schema of a `Page.Defer` prop (`Deferred<T>` in C#): a thenable for React's `use()` whose value is validated by `schema` when it arrives. A value that does not match rejects with `Invalid deferred value: ...`, which reaches the error boundary. The generated schemas use it for every `Deferred<T>` property. It returns the same thenable for the same value and schema on every render, so `use()` does not suspend again.

#### `DeferredValue`

```ts
class DeferredValue<T> implements PromiseLike<T> {
  status: 'pending' | 'fulfilled' | 'rejected';
  value?: T;
  reason?: unknown;
  constructor(source: PromiseLike<unknown>, parse: (value: unknown) => T);
  then<R1 = T, R2 = never>(onFulfilled?: ..., onRejected?: ...): PromiseLike<R1 | R2>;
}
```

The value `deferred()` parses to: a thenable that records `status`, `value` and `reason` the way React's `use()` reads them. It is not a `Promise`, which would make zod treat the whole schema as async. A value nobody reads does not surface as an unhandled rejection.

## `netjes/testing`

The harness for testing components and pages with Vitest and Testing Library ([Testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/testing.md)). The router in it is a fake: it records what the component asked for and moves to the new URL, but loads nothing.

#### `createTestApp`

```ts
function createTestApp(options?: TestAppOptions): TestApp;

type TestAppOptions = {
  url?: string;                     // the current URL, default '/'
  route?: string;                   // the page's pattern, e.g. '/blog/[slug]'
  params?: Params;                  // what useParams() returns
  shared?: unknown;                 // what useSharedProps() returns
  publicConfig?: Record<string, unknown>; // what usePublicConfig() returns
  locale?: string;                  // what useLocale() returns
  draftMode?: boolean;              // what useDraftMode() reports
  queries?: ReadonlyArray<{ key: readonly unknown[]; data: unknown }>; // seeded as .WithQuery seeds them
  defaultOptions?: DefaultOptions;  // like netjes({ query: { defaultOptions } }); retries are off
  queryClient?: QueryClient;        // use this client instead of a new one
  navigation?: NavigationState;     // what useNavigation() returns, default idle
  antiforgery?: AntiforgeryToken | false; // the token <Form method="post"> adds; false for none
  actions?: Record<string, (input: unknown) => TestActionAnswer | Promise<TestActionAnswer>>;
};

type TestApp = {
  Wrapper: (props: { children: ReactNode }) => ReactNode; // pass as Testing Library's `wrapper`
  navigations: TestNavigation[];                           // every navigation, router call and post, in order
  queryClient: QueryClient;
};

type TestNavigation =
  | { type: 'push' | 'replace'; href: string }
  | { type: 'refresh' | 'back' | 'forward' }
  | { type: 'submit'; action: string; data: URLSearchParams | FormData }
  | { type: 'action'; name: string; input: unknown };

type TestActionAnswer = ActionState<unknown> & {
  queries?: ReadonlyArray<{ key: readonly unknown[]; data: unknown }>; // set, as .WithQuery does
  invalidate?: ReadonlyArray<readonly unknown[]>;                      // invalidated, as .Invalidate does
  fields?: readonly string[]; // after a failure: the fields `values` keeps, as the server names them (default all)
};
```

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createTestApp } from 'netjes/testing';

const app = createTestApp({
  actions: { 'home.greet': () => ({ ok: false, status: 422, errors: { name: ['Tell us your name.'] } }) },
});
render(<HelloForm />, { wrapper: app.Wrapper });
await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Say hello' }));
expect(await screen.findByText('Tell us your name.')).toBeDefined();
```

Links and `router.push` move to the new URL, so hooks see it, and are recorded. Form posts are recorded with their fields. Server action calls are recorded and answered by `actions[name]`; an action without an answer succeeds with no result. Components inside the `Wrapper` can call actions from the effects they run as they mount, layout effects included; a call outside any `Wrapper` throws at once ([answering server actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/testing.md#answering-server-actions)). The default antiforgery token is a test token, and the `QueryClient` has retries off.

## `netjes/testing/setup`

A Vitest setup file that runs Testing Library's `cleanup()` after each test. The `netjes()` plugin registers it when `@testing-library/react` is installed and the app's Vitest config sets no `setupFiles` of its own; list it in `setupFiles` yourself when it does.

## `netjes/vitals`

Core Web Vitals, measured with the `web-vitals` package, which the app installs (`npm install web-vitals`).

#### `useReportWebVitals`

```ts
function useReportWebVitals(callback: (metric: WebVitalsMetric) => void): void;

type WebVitalsMetric = Pick<Metric, 'name' | 'value' | 'rating' | 'delta' | 'id' | 'navigationType'> & { route: string | null };
```

Calls back with each Core Web Vital of the page load (CLS, FCP, INP, LCP, TTFB), with the route pattern of the page the document was loaded on, like Next.js's `useReportWebVitals`. A component that subscribes late also gets the metrics measured before it.

#### `WebVitals`

```ts
function WebVitals(): null;
```

Sends the page load's Core Web Vitals to the server with `navigator.sendBeacon`, which records them as `netjes.web_vitals.*` histograms when `NetjesOptions.CollectWebVitals` is on; without it, it sends nothing. Each measurement is sent once, even when the component unmounts and mounts again. Render it once, in the root layout. See [Deployment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/deployment.md).

## `netjes/vite`

```ts
export default function netjes(options?: NetjesPluginOptions): PluginOption[];
```

The Vite plugin: React, Tailwind CSS, the page module map, the query client, Vitest defaults, and the client and server builds. Its options are in [Vite plugin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/vite-plugin.md).

## Internal entry points

These are exported for the plugin and the .NET app; app code does not import them.

| Import | What it is |
|---|---|
| `netjes/client-entry` | The browser entry the plugin builds: it reads the page payload, hydrates the document (or renders it, when no sidecar was ready to render it on the server) and receives streamed deferred values. |
| `netjes/server-entry` | The server entry: `render` and `renderToStream`, which the sidecar calls with a page payload. |
| `netjes/sidecar` | The Node sidecar, `sidecar/server.mjs`, which the .NET app starts and supervises. |

## The generated module

`generated/netjes.ts` is written from the app's C# types and page files by the app in Development and by `netjes generate` ([Generated types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md#generated-types)). Next to a zod schema and a type per C# type, it exports:

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `pages` | Each page's props schema by pattern, for `definePage`. |
| `layouts` | Each layout loader's props schema by folder, for `defineLayout`. Only when the app has layout loaders. |
| `sharedProps` | The shared props schema, for `useSharedProps`; `z.unknown()` without `UseSharedProps<T>`. |
| `api` | `{ request?, response? }` schemas of each JSON minimal API, keyed `'GET /api/...'`. |
| `forms` | The `[FromForm]` schema of each page action, by pattern. |
| `serverActions` | A typed `ServerAction` per `MapAction`, by name. Only when the app has server actions. |
| `route(pattern, params?, search?)` | The URL of a page, values encoded, typed by pattern. |
| `Route` | The URLs the pages serve, as template literal types. |
| `Href` | `Route` with a query or fragment, `?…`, `#…`, and `http(s):`, `mailto:` and `tel:` URLs; also a zod schema of the same name, for `Href.parse(value)`. |
| `isHref(value)` | Whether a string is an `Href`. |
| `RouteParams`, `RoutePattern`, `routePatterns` | The parameters per pattern, the patterns as a type, and as an array. |

TanStack Query's hooks (`useQuery`, `useMutation`, `useQueryClient` and the rest) come straight from `@tanstack/react-query`; Netjes provides the client ([Server state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md#server-state-with-tanstack-query)).

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/csharp-api.md -->

# C# API

This page lists the public API of the `Netjes` and `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp` NuGet packages: every public type and extension method, grouped by what it is for, each with its signature and what it does. It is a reference for app developers; the guides show how the pieces fit together. Options are listed separately, in the [options reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/reference/options.md).

Extension methods live in the namespaces of what they extend, which a web project imports already: `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder` (`UseNetjes`, `MapPages`, `MapPageLoader`, ...), `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` (`AddNetjes`, ...), `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting` and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http`; the sitemap's are in `Netjes`. The types are in `Netjes`, which the package's build targets import into projects with implicit usings, and in `Netjes.Images`, `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp`, `Netjes.Rendering` and `Netjes.Routing`.

The extension methods belong to these static classes, which app code never names:

| Class | Namespace | Methods |
|---|---|---|
| `NetjesServiceCollectionExtensions` | `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` | `AddNetjes` on `IServiceCollection` and on `IHealthChecksBuilder` |
| `NetjesApplicationBuilderExtensions` | `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder` | `UseNetjes` |
| `NetjesEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions` | `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder` | `MapPages`, `MapPageLoader`, `MapLayoutLoader`, `MapPageAction`, `MapAction`, `CachePage` |
| `StaticExportEndpointConventionBuilderExtensions` | `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder` | `StaticParams`, `ExcludeFromExport` |
| `NetjesLocalizationServiceCollectionExtensions` | `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` | `AddNetjesLocalization` |
| `NetjesLocalizationApplicationBuilderExtensions` | `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder` | `UseNetjesLocalization`, `MapLocaleRedirect` |
| `NetjesHostExtensions` | `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting` | `GetNetjesCommand` |
| `NetjesHttpContextExtensions` | `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http` | `GetCspNonce` |
| `SitemapEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions` | `Netjes` | `MapSitemap`, `MapRobotsTxt`, `ExcludeFromSitemap` |
| `SkiaImagesServiceCollectionExtensions` | `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` (package `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp`) | `AddNetjesSkiaImages` |

## Setting up

### AddNetjes

```csharp
public static IServiceCollection AddNetjes(this IServiceCollection services, Action<NetjesOptions>? configure = null)
```

Registers Netjes: options bound from the `Netjes` configuration section and then `configure`, antiforgery, the sidecar pool, the renderer, type generation, the route warnings, the export command, draft mode, the image endpoint's services and the output-cache rules for pages. Pair it with `UseNetjes()` and `MapPages()`.

### UseNetjes

```csharp
public static IApplicationBuilder UseNetjes(this IApplicationBuilder app)
```
