- `appType` is `'custom'`: the .NET app serves the documents, and Vite serves modules.

### TypeScript setup

`netjes` ships its modules as JavaScript with declaration files (`.d.ts`), so the app's `tsc` checks the app's own code against the declarations of `netjes`, not against its sources. The app may add stricter compiler options, such as `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` or `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature`: the declarations pass under them, with `skipLibCheck` on or off. They resolve under `moduleResolution` `bundler` (the template's), `node16` and `nodenext`, which read the package's `exports`.

The TypeScript sources ship in the package too: the declaration maps and source maps point at them, so an editor's go to definition and a stack trace lead to the TypeScript.

### Vitest defaults

Under Vitest, unless `test` is `false`, the plugin sets these, each only if the app's own `test` config leaves it unset:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `environment` | `'jsdom'`, when `jsdom` is installed |
| `exclude` | `node_modules`, `dist`, `bin`, `obj`, `e2e` (for Playwright) and `.git` folders |
| `setupFiles` | A setup file that unmounts what each test rendered (Testing Library's `cleanup`), when `@testing-library/react` is installed |

It sets no `include`, so Vitest's own pattern (`*.test.*` and `*.spec.*` files) applies outside those folders. Tests then render with `createTestApp()` from `netjes/testing`; see [Testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/guides/testing.md).

## The dev server

In development the .NET app starts a Node process that runs the Vite dev server with this config, and renders pages through it. The browser loads modules and hot updates from that server, on its own port.

- It listens on port 5173, which `Netjes:ViteDevPort` changes, with `strictPort`: the browser loads modules and hot updates from that port, so when something else has it the dev server does not move to another one. The app logs that the port is in use and how to move Vite (`Netjes__ViteDevPort=5174`), in one line, and stops with exit code 1; `netjes dev` checks the port before it starts the app.
- When it does not start for another reason, such as an error in `vite.config.ts` or a package the config imports that is not installed, the app logs what Vite reported, its code frame included, and what to do (`npm install` for a package it cannot find), in one log entry, and stops with exit code 1.
- It binds to `localhost`. `NETJES_VITE_HOST=0.0.0.0` in the environment of `npm run dev` exposes it to the network, as the template's development container does; `NETJES_VITE_ORIGIN` sets the origin the browser uses, when it reaches the server by another address.
- It may read files from the workspace root, unless your config sets `server.fs.allow`, and from the `netjes` package.

The dev server's root is the app's folder, which also holds the .NET side, so the plugin denies these to the dev server, on top of Vite's own defaults (`.env`, `.env.*`, certificates and `.git`):

- `appsettings*.json`, `launchSettings.json`, `secrets.json`, `nuget.config` and `*.user` files;
- `*.cs`, `*.csproj`, `*.pdb` and `*.dll` files, `Directory.Build.*` and `global.json`;
- dev certificates and keys (`*.pfx`, `*.p12`, `*.key`) and SQLite databases (`*.db`, `*.sqlite`, `*.sqlite3`);
- Compose files (`compose*.yml`, `docker-compose*.yml`, and `.yaml`);
- the `bin/`, `obj/` and `dist/server/` folders below the workspace root.

A `server.fs.deny` of your own is added to that list. Everything else under the allowed folders is readable by anyone who can reach the port, which is why the server binds to localhost: expose it only on a network you trust.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/README.md -->

# netjes

The npm half of [Netjes](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes), a React framework for building apps and sites on ASP.NET Core: pages in `app/` with the Next.js App Router conventions, C# loaders and server actions, server rendering, client navigation. This package holds the Vite plugin, the client router and components, the Node sidecar that renders pages for the .NET app, the `netjes` command and the app template. The ASP.NET Core half is the [`Netjes`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Netjes) NuGet package, released at the same version.

## Start an app

You need Node.js `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0` (Node.js 22.22.2 or a later 22, 24.15.0 or a later 24, or 26 or newer) and the .NET 10 SDK.

```bash
npx netjes new my-app
cd my-app
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5080
```

`netjes new` writes an ASP.NET Core app with React pages, Tailwind CSS, TanStack Query, zod, Vitest and Docker files, and references `netjes` and `Netjes` at the same exact version.

## Add it to a project

```bash
npm install netjes@0.0.1 react react-dom zod @tanstack/react-query
npm install -D vite tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import netjes from 'netjes/vite';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [netjes()] });
```

Tailwind CSS and the TanStack Query client are on by default; `netjes({ tailwind: false, query: false })` turns them off, and then they need not be installed. `vitest`, `jsdom`, `@testing-library/react` and `web-vitals` are optional peers, used when installed. Use the version of `netjes` that matches the app's `Netjes` NuGet package; `npx netjes info` checks it.

## Entry points

| Import | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `netjes` | Components and hooks: `Link`, `Form`, `Image`, `Script`, `definePage`, `useAction`, `useRouter` and the rest |
| `netjes/vite` | The Vite plugin |
| `netjes/testing` | `createTestApp()`, for rendering pages and components in Vitest |
| `netjes/vitals` | `useReportWebVitals` and `<WebVitals />` |
| `netjes/zod` | `deferred(schema)`, for values that loaders stream with `Page.Defer` |
| `netjes` (bin) | The command: `new`, `dev`, `build`, `start`, `generate`, `routes`, `export`, `info`, `agents` |

Each import is an ES module with its type declarations, so an app's `tsc` reads the declarations and checks only the app's own code, also under stricter compiler options such as `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` or `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature` (see [TypeScript setup](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/vite-plugin.md#typescript-setup)). The TypeScript sources are in the package too, for the source maps: an editor's go to definition and a stack trace lead to them.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)
- [All guides](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/README.md)
- [React API](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/react-api.md)
- [Vite plugin](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/vite-plugin.md)
- [The netjes command](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/cli.md)

Report bugs in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/issues), and security problems privately, as [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/SECURITY.md) describes. MIT licensed.

# Netjes

The ASP.NET Core half of [Netjes](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes), a React framework for building apps and sites on ASP.NET Core. Pages live in `app/` with the Next.js App Router conventions; this package turns them into endpoints, runs their C# loaders and server actions, renders them through a supervised pool of Node processes, and handles caching, images and the generated TypeScript types. The npm package [`netjes`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/netjes), released at the same version, is the other half: the Vite plugin, the client router and the renderer.

## Start an app

```bash
npx netjes new my-app
```

That writes an app with both halves set up. To add Netjes to a project you have, reference this package and install the npm half at the same version (0.0.1 here; the two are released together):

```bash
dotnet add package Netjes --version 0.0.1
npm install netjes@0.0.1 react react-dom zod @tanstack/react-query
```

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc; // for [FromForm]

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddNetjes();

var app = builder.Build();
app.UseNetjes();
app.UseAntiforgery(); // after authentication, if you have it

app.MapPageLoader("/", (TimeProvider time) => Page.Props(new HomeProps("Hello from C#", time.GetUtcNow())));
app.MapAction("home.greet", ([FromForm] GreetInput input) => ServerAction.Ok(new Greeting($"Hello, {input.Name}!")));
app.MapPages(); // every other page file, plus the 404 fallback

app.Run();

public sealed record HomeProps(string Message, DateTimeOffset RenderedAt);
public sealed record GreetInput { public string? Name { get; init; } }
public sealed record Greeting(string Text);
```

The package adds build targets to the project: `using Netjes` when implicit usings are on, `node_modules` and `dist` kept out of the build, and `dotnet publish` running `npm run build` and shipping `dist/`. The app needs the .NET 10 SDK and, at build time and in production, Node.js `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0` (Node.js 22.22.2 or a later 22, 24.15.0 or a later 24, or 26 or newer).

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)
- [All guides](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/README.md)
- [C# API](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/csharp-api.md)
- [Options](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/options.md)
- [Architecture](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/architecture.md)

Report bugs in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/issues), and security problems privately, as [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/SECURITY.md) describes. MIT licensed.

# Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp

Image processing for the [Netjes](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Netjes) `<Image>` endpoint, built on SkiaSharp (MIT). Without it the endpoint serves originals (cached); with it, images are resized to the requested width, never larger than the source, and encoded as WebP.

## Install

```bash
dotnet add package Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp --version 0.0.1
```

```csharp
builder.Services.AddNetjes();
builder.Services.AddNetjesSkiaImages();   // before or after AddNetjes()
```

Options:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddNetjesSkiaImages(o =>
{
    o.MaxPixels = 40_000_000;                    // refuse images whose header declares more (default)
    o.MaxConcurrency = Environment.ProcessorCount; // images decoded and encoded at once (default)
});
```

## What it does

- Decodes PNG, JPEG and WebP only, and only bytes that start with the declared format's signature. Output is WebP when the browser accepts it, otherwise JPEG and WebP sources keep their format and PNG stays PNG.
- Applies the EXIF orientation, and decodes large JPEGs at a reduced size.
- GIFs (possibly animated) and AVIFs pass through unchanged. Every other format (BMP and ICO, for example), bytes that do not match their declared format, and images that fail to decode are refused, not passed through.
- Images whose header declares more than `MaxPixels` are refused before decoding (refused like any other image it cannot process), since a small file can claim a huge size.
- A refused image answers 400 from the endpoint when it is a local file and 502 when it is a remote image (the remote host supplied bad bytes).
- Linux builds use `SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux.NoDependencies`, so it runs in the slim ASP.NET Core images.

## Security

This package decodes bytes that visitors and remote hosts control, with native codecs (libjpeg-turbo, libpng, libwebp and others inside SkiaSharp's Skia build). Native image codecs have a history of memory-safety vulnerabilities, so keep the SkiaSharp packages current: update `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp` and watch SkiaSharp releases and advisories. The pixel limit and concurrency cap bound resource use but do not protect against a codec bug. Restrict `Netjes:Images:RemoteHosts` to hosts you trust and leave `AllowSvg` off.

Use the same version as `Netjes` (0.0.1 above); the two are released together. The [images guide](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/images.md) covers `<Image>`, the endpoint's limits and `IImageProcessor`. MIT licensed.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/SKILL.md -->

# Building a Netjes app

Netjes renders React pages from ASP.NET Core. C# receives every request and owns routing, loaders, server actions, authorization and caching. A Node sidecar renders the React tree to HTML; the browser hydrates it, and later navigations fetch the next page's props as JSON from the same C# endpoints. The file conventions in `app/` are the Next.js App Router's, but there are no React Server Components and no `route.ts`: data comes from C# loaders, and APIs are minimal API endpoints.

## Where things go

- `app/**/page.tsx`: a page. `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` serves `/blog/{slug}`. Layouts, boundaries and folder rules: [references/routing.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/routing.md).
- `Features/<Feature>/*.cs`: the C# side of a feature, mapped by an extension method that `Program.cs` calls before `app.MapPages()`. Loaders and actions: [references/data-and-actions.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/data-and-actions.md).
- `generated/netjes.ts`: zod schemas and typed references generated from the C# types and the page files. Read it to see what a page receives; never edit it.
- `components/`: React components and their tests. Testing: [references/testing.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/testing.md).

## The loop for any change

1. Write the failing test first: a Vitest component test, or a C# test for loader and action logic.
2. Change the C# record, loader or action, then run `npx netjes generate` so `generated/netjes.ts` matches (a running `npm run dev` rewrites it when it restarts).
3. Use the generated names in React: `pages['/pattern']`, `layouts['app/folder']`, `serverActions['name']`, `api['GET /api/...']`, `route('/pattern', params)`.
4. Check: `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `dotnet build` (warnings are errors), `npx netjes generate --check`, and `npm run routes` for route warnings.

## A page with data, end to end

```csharp
// Features/Posts/PostPages.cs
namespace MyApp.Features.Posts;

public static class PostPages
{
    public sealed record PostProps(string Slug, string Title, string Body);

    public static void MapPostPages(this IEndpointRouteBuilder app)
    {
        // The parameter name matches [slug]; Page.Props names the props type for the generated schema.
        app.MapPageLoader("/blog/[slug]", (string slug, PostStore posts) =>
            posts.Find(slug) is { } post
                ? Page.Props(new PostProps(post.Slug, post.Title, post.Body))
                    .WithMetadata(new PageMetadata { Title = post.Title })
                : Page.NotFound());
    }
}
```

```tsx
// app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx
import { Link, definePage } from 'netjes';
import { pages, route } from '../../../generated/netjes.ts';

export default definePage(pages['/blog/[slug]'], function Post({ title, body }) {
  return (
    <article>
      <Link href={route('/blog')}>All posts</Link>
      <h1>{title}</h1>
      <p>{body}</p>
    </article>
  );
});
```

`Program.cs` calls `app.MapPostPages();` before `app.MapPages();`. A page without a loader is a plain default export with no props.

## Rules

- Decisions live in C#: data access, validation, authorization (`.RequireAuthorization()`, `Page.Forbidden()`), redirects, caching. React renders what it is sent.
- Loaders and actions return Netjes results (`Page.Props(...)`, `Page.NotFound()`, `ServerAction.Ok(...)`), so their types reach `generated/netjes.ts`. Use records for everything that crosses to the browser.
- zod at every boundary: `definePage`/`defineLayout` with the generated schemas, `useSearchParams(schema)` and `useParams(schema)` (schemas at module level), `api[...].response.parse(...)` for fetched JSON, `usePublicConfig(schema)`. No `any`, no casts of server data.
- Server state goes through TanStack Query, seeded from the loader with `.WithQuery(key, data)`; no `useEffect` fetching.
- Internal links use `<Link>` and `route()`; forms use `<Form>` with `useAction`, and must work without JavaScript.
- Never edit `generated/netjes.ts`; regenerate it and commit it with the change.
- Anything in `Netjes:PublicConfig` or shared props is sent to the browser.
- Caching, streaming and static export have sharp edges: read [references/caching-and-streaming.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/caching-and-streaming.md) before using `.CachePage`, `Page.Defer` or `netjes export`.
- Shipping: [references/deployment.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/deployment.md).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | `dotnet watch` with Vite HMR on http://localhost:5080 |
| `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` | Vitest; strict TypeScript |
| `npx netjes generate [--check]` | Rewrite `generated/netjes.ts`; `--check` fails when it is stale |
| `npm run routes` (`netjes routes [--json]`) | The route table and route warnings, as ASP.NET Core sees them |
| `npx netjes build` | Types, then the client and server bundles |
| `npx netjes start` | Run in Production |
| `npx netjes export [dir]` | Write the site as static HTML |
| `npx netjes info` | Versions and a check of the project setup |

## More

The guides go further than these references: [routing](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/routing.md), [data loading](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md), [actions and forms](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md), [metadata](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/metadata.md), [images](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/images.md), [rendering and streaming](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/rendering-and-streaming.md), [caching](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/caching.md), [security](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/security.md), [testing](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/testing.md) and [deployment](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/deployment.md), with the [React API](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/react-api.md), the [C# API](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/csharp-api.md) and the [options](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/options.md) as reference.

The same docs as plain text: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/llms.txt (an index) and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/llms-full.txt (everything in one file). They follow the main branch; the installed version's sources and types are in `node_modules/netjes/`.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/routing.md -->

# Routing

ASP.NET Core does the routing: every page file becomes an endpoint with an ordinary route template, so precedence, constraints and conventions such as `RequireAuthorization()` work as for any minimal API. The browser never matches routes itself.

## Files in `app/`

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `page.tsx` | The page for its folder's URL. |
| `layout.tsx` | Wraps every page below it and stays mounted across navigations (its state survives). The root `app/layout.tsx` imports the global stylesheet. |
| `template.tsx` | Like a layout, but remounted on every navigation. |
| `loading.tsx` | Suspense fallback, streamed first while the page below waits on deferred values or lazy code. |
| `error.tsx` | Error boundary below its layout; props `{ error, reset }` (`ErrorPageProps`), status in `error.status`. In development `error.message` can take several lines (a syntax error's code frame): render it with `whitespace-pre-wrap`. |
| `not-found.tsx` | Rendered for `Page.NotFound()` from a loader below it, and the root one for unknown URLs. |
| `forbidden.tsx`, `unauthorized.tsx` | Rendered for `Page.Forbidden()` / `Page.Unauthorized()` and for empty 403/401 responses from authorization; without one, the error page renders. |
| `global-error.tsx` | In `app/` only: rendered without any layout when even the error page fails. |

Built-in pages stand in for missing boundary files.

## Folders

| Folder | URL |
|---|---|
| `blog/[slug]` | `/blog/{slug}`: one segment |
| `docs/[...path]` | `/docs/a/b`: one or more segments; the loader gets them joined by `/` |
| `docs/[[...path]]` | `/docs` and anything below it |
| `(group)` | No URL segment: groups pages under a shared layout (`app/(marketing)/layout.tsx`) |
| `_private` | Not routed: components that live next to the pages |
| `@slot` + `default.tsx` | A parallel route: the layout gets the slot as a prop |
| `@modal/(.)photo/[id]` | An intercepting route, inside a slot only: a client navigation shows it in the slot, a reload shows the real page |

A literal segment beats a dynamic one (`blog/new` over `blog/[slug]`), as in Next.js. Two page files of the same shape (`[lang]/about` and `[slug]/about`) stop the app at startup. There is no pages router: Next.js pages router files in `pages/` stop the app at startup, and the message says where each goes (`pages/about.js` to `app/about/page.jsx`, `pages/404.tsx` to `app/not-found.tsx`, `pages/_app.tsx` and `pages/_document.tsx` to the root `app/layout.tsx`, `pages/api/` routes to minimal API endpoints). There are no route handlers either: a `route.ts` in `app/` stops the app in development and fails `vite build`, and an API is a minimal API endpoint in C# (`app.MapGet`, `app.MapPost`).

## Loader parameters and route warnings

Loaders bind like minimal APIs: a string or `TryParse` parameter takes the route value of the same name (any case), and otherwise the query string. `(string id)` on `/blog/[slug]` therefore reads `?id=`, never the slug, and `string[] path` on `[...path]` reads `?path=`. Netjes logs a warning for that at startup, and `npm run routes` prints it. Name parameters after the route segment, or mark query parameters `[FromQuery]`. The other warning is two pages that match the same URLs (`[id]` next to `[...rest]`); rename one, or accept it if the overlap is wanted.

## Links and navigation

- `<Link href={route('/blog/[slug]', { slug })}>`: client navigation with prefetch on hover and focus, `aria-current` on the active link. `route()` and the `Href` type come from `generated/netjes.ts`, so a wrong path or a missing parameter is a type error.
- `useRouter()`: `push`, `replace`, `prefetch`, `refresh`, `back`, `forward`.
- `usePathname()`, `useSearchParams(schema?)`, `useParams(schema?)`: with a schema the values are parsed; catch-all params are arrays. Search values a schema rejects are dropped so its defaults apply; a rejected route param goes to the error page, so constrain route params in C#.
- `useSelectedLayoutSegment()`, `useSelectedLayoutSegments()`: the active child segment in a layout (tabs).
- `useNavigation()`: `idle`, `loading` or `submitting`, for progress indicators.
- External URLs, `target`, `download` and modified clicks behave like a plain `<a>`; `reloadDocument` forces a full load.

## Metadata

- `export const metadata: Metadata = { title: 'About' }` on pages and layouts; a layout's `title: { default, template: '%s · Site' }` applies to the pages below it.
- From C#: `.WithMetadata(new PageMetadata { Title = post.Title, Description = ... })` on the loader's result, merged over the files' metadata.
- Below a layout that sets a title, use `metadata`, not a `<title>` element (that makes a second title).

## Protecting sections

`app.MapLayoutLoader("/dashboard", ...).RequireAuthorization()` protects every page below `app/dashboard/`; `app.MapPages().RequireAuthorization()` protects every page that has no loader of its own; a page loader takes `.RequireAuthorization()` itself. With cookie authentication, answer 401/403 instead of redirecting (`OnRedirectToLogin`, `OnRedirectToAccessDenied`) so `unauthorized.tsx` and `forbidden.tsx` render.

A check that depends on data (is this user a member of this project?) goes in the page loader as well as in the layout loader: a page's loader runs before its layouts' loaders, and a layout loader is skipped on client navigations within its section while its own route values, the user and the roles stay the same. A layout loader also binds only the route values of its own URL, so it cannot check a deeper one.

## Base path and locales

`app.UsePathBase("/docs")` with `netjes({ basePath: '/docs' })`; links, forms and redirects add it, and app code is written as if at the root (`useHref(path)` for a plain `<a>`). Locale routing is a `[lang]` folder with `AddNetjesLocalization`, `UseNetjesLocalization` and `MapLocaleRedirect`; `useLocale()` reads it.

## More

[Routing](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/routing.md) and [Metadata](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/metadata.md) in the guides, and the [React API](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/react-api.md) for every component and hook.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/data-and-actions.md -->

# Data and actions

Everything a page shows comes from C#: page loaders, layout loaders, shared props and JSON endpoints. Everything a page changes goes through C#: server actions. Their C# types become zod schemas and typed references in `generated/netjes.ts`.

## Page loaders

```csharp
app.MapPageLoader("/projects/[id]", async (string id, ClaimsPrincipal user, AppDb db, CancellationToken ct) =>
{
    var project = await db.FindProjectAsync(id, ct);
    if (project is null) return Page.NotFound();
    if (!project.HasMember(user)) return Page.Forbidden();
    return Page.Props(new ProjectProps(project.Name, project.Tasks))
        .WithQuery(["projects", id, "stats"], await db.StatsAsync(id, ct))
        .WithMetadata(new PageMetadata { Title = project.Name });
});
```

- It binds like a minimal API: route values by name, services, `ClaimsPrincipal`, `HttpContext`, `CancellationToken`, `[FromQuery]`.
- It reads no request body, so a complex type that is not a registered service needs `[AsParameters]` or a static `BindAsync`. A loader or action whose parameters minimal APIs cannot bind stops the app at startup, saying which and why. So does a loader parameter that reads the body (`[FromBody]`, `[FromForm]`, `IFormFile`): posted data belongs in a page action or a server action. A page loader stops the app too for a type that adds accepts metadata (`IAcceptsMetadata`) for itself, and must not get `.Accepts<T>()`: routing would match the page only for requests with that Content-Type, and navigations would get the not-found page. Repeated query values bind to an array (`int[] ids`); `List<int>` and `IEnumerable<int>` stop the app at startup, the latter because minimal APIs would bind it from services.
- `Page.Props(record)` names the props type for `pages['/projects/[id]']`. `Page.NotFound()`, `Page.Forbidden()`, `Page.Unauthorized()` render the nearest boundary file; `Page.Redirect(url)` and `Page.LocalRedirect(returnUrl)` (for URLs from the request) redirect, and the client router follows them. `.WithStatus(422)` changes the status.
- It returns a `RouteHandlerBuilder`: `.RequireAuthorization()`, `.CachePage(...)` and filters apply.
- A page's loader runs before its layouts' loaders, so a page under a layout that checks access checks it too.

## Layout loaders

`app.MapLayoutLoader("/projects/[id]", ...)` loads the data of `app/.../projects/[id]/layout.tsx` (by URL, or by folder: `app/(shop)`). The layout reads it with `defineLayout(layouts['app/(app)/projects/[id]'], function Layout({ project, children }) { ... })`. Its conventions (`.RequireAuthorization()`) apply to every page below. `NotFound`/`Forbidden` from it render the nearest boundary above the layout.

- It binds only the route values of its own URL (`id` here, never a deeper `taskId`; a `[FromRoute]` naming one stops the app at startup), the query string and services. Nothing binds from a body: a complex type needs to be a service, `[AsParameters]` or bind itself, and `[FromBody]`, `[FromForm]` or a file stops the app at startup.
- On client navigations within the section it is skipped while its route values, user and roles are unchanged, so checks that must run on every request belong in conventions or page loaders, and it must not depend on the query string or cookies.

## Shared props

`options.UseSharedProps(http => ValueTask.FromResult(new SiteProps(...)))` in `AddNetjes` gives every page and layout the same props: `useSharedProps(sharedProps)`. Typical: the signed-in user, from `http.User`. They are sent to the browser.

## Server actions

```csharp
using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc; // [FromForm]: not in the implicit usings

public sealed record Renamed(string Name);

public sealed record RenameInput
{
    [Required] public string Id { get; init; } = "";
    [Required(ErrorMessage = "Give it a name."), StringLength(100)] public string Name { get; init; } = "";
}

app.MapAction("projects.rename", async ([FromForm] RenameInput input, AppDb db, CancellationToken ct) =>
    await db.TryRenameAsync(input.Id, input.Name, ct)
        ? ServerAction.Ok(new Renamed(input.Name)).RevalidatePath($"/projects/{input.Id}")
        : ServerAction.Invalid("name", "That name is taken."));
```

```tsx
const [state, formAction, pending] = useAction(serverActions['projects.rename']);
const nameError = state?.ok === false ? state.errors.name?.[0] : undefined;

<Form action={formAction}>
  <input type="hidden" name="id" value={id} />
  <input name="name" defaultValue={state?.ok === false ? String(state.values?.name ?? '') : name} aria-invalid={nameError ? true : undefined} />
  {nameError && <p>{nameError}</p>}
  <button disabled={pending}>Rename</button>
</Form>
```

- Results: `ServerAction.Ok(result)` or `Ok()`, `Invalid(field, message)` or `Invalid(errors)` (422), `Redirect(url)`, `Forbidden()`, `NotFound()`. Chain `.Revalidate(tags)` and `.RevalidatePath(paths)` (evict output-cached pages and refresh the page), `.Refresh()`, `.Invalidate(queryKey)` and `.WithQuery(queryKey, data)` (TanStack Query on the client).
- `[FromForm]` inputs make the form work without JavaScript: the browser posts, a success redirects back, a failure renders the page again with the errors and the typed values. Keep that working.
- An input without `[FromForm]` binds JSON: `await serverActions['posts.like']({ slug })` resolves to `{ ok: true, result }` or `{ ok: false, errors }`; server failures throw to the nearest error boundary.
- Validation: DataAnnotations (`[Required]`, `[StringLength]`, `[Range]`, `[EmailAddress]`) and `IValidatableObject` on an action's input are checked before the action runs (for a polymorphic JSON input, those of the `[JsonDerivedType]` the call sends). Failures come back as field errors (422, `state.errors`), also without JavaScript, and the action is not called. This needs no setup: `builder.Services.AddValidation()` is for your other minimal API endpoints, not for `MapAction` or `MapPageAction`. An attribute that cannot be read, such as a `[Display]` whose resource type has no such name, stops the app at startup, also on a derived type a JSON input lists with `[JsonDerivedType]`. A `[FromForm]` input is never `null` (unless declared nullable): a post with none of its fields, such as a form of unchecked checkboxes, gets an empty input, checked like any other. Give form inputs `init` properties, as above, not constructor parameters: a field the post leaves out (an unchecked checkbox, a list with nothing chosen) keeps its default, while form binding refuses such a post (400) for a positional record. A form input, and each type its properties and lists hold, needs exactly one public constructor: form binding never builds a type with several or none, or an abstract class or an interface, so that stops the app at startup. Bind a checkbox group or a list as a property of the input type (`public string[] Tags { get; init; } = [];`), not as a top-level `[FromForm]` parameter: a top-level list or dictionary reads fields named `[0]` or `[key]`, not its own name, and is `null` when none is posted.
- Optimistic UI: `useAction(action, { onSubmit(formData) { setOptimistic(...) } })` with React's `useOptimistic`.
- Every action needs `app.UseAntiforgery()` (after authentication) and checks the origin; `<Form>` and `serverActions` send the token. `MapAction` bodies are limited to 1 MB (`ActionBodySizeLimit`); an upload action sets `[RequestSizeLimit(bytes)]`. Page actions keep the server's limit.
- Name actions `feature.verb`. Check authorization inside the action, or with `.RequireAuthorization()`, as for any endpoint.
- `app.MapPageAction("/guestbook", ...)` is the other kind: a POST to the page's own URL from `<Form method="post">`, fields typed in `forms['/guestbook']`. Its input's DataAnnotations and `IValidatableObject` are checked as for `MapAction`: on a failure the delegate does not run, the page renders again from its loader (422), and `const failed = usePageActionState()` gives `failed.errors` and `failed.values` (null otherwise). Checks that need data stay in the delegate: return `Page.Props(...)` with your own errors and the typed values (`.WithStatus(422)`), or `Page.Redirect(...)` after a change.
- An action or post that sets or deletes a cookie (signing in or out) makes the client router forget the pages it keeps for back and forward, reload the page on screen and clear the query cache, in every tab of the app in that browser. Nothing to do in the action; a proxy must pass `X-Netjes-Cookies` through.

## JSON endpoints and TanStack Query

```csharp
app.MapGet("/api/projects/{slug}/stats", async Task<Results<Ok<ProjectStats>, NotFound>> (string slug, AppDb db) => ...)
    .RequireAuthorization();
```

```ts
async function fetchStats(slug: string) {
  const response = await fetch(`/api/projects/${encodeURIComponent(slug)}/stats`);
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Stats request failed with ${response.status}`);
  return api['GET /api/projects/{slug}/stats'].response.parse(await response.json());
}
const stats = useQuery({ queryKey: ['projects', slug, 'stats'], queryFn: () => fetchStats(slug) });
```

Typed results (`TypedResults`, `Results<...>`) give the endpoint its `api` schemas, keyed by method and route template. Seed the same query key from the loader with `.WithQuery(key, data)` and the query renders on the server with no fetch; keep the key in one place on each side. Seeded data is fresh for the default `staleTime` (one minute).

## More

[Data loading](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/data-loading.md) and [Actions and forms](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/actions-and-forms.md) in the guides.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/caching-and-streaming.md -->

# Caching, streaming and static export

## Output-cached pages

```csharp
builder.Services.AddOutputCache();
// ...
app.UseNetjes();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();
app.UseAntiforgery();
app.UseOutputCache();          // after UseNetjes and after UseAuthentication, so signed-in users bypass it

app.MapPageLoader("/blog/[slug]", (string slug, PostStore posts) => ...)
    .CachePage(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5), "posts");
```

- A stored page is served to every visitor, shared props included. Cache only pages that are the same for everyone: their loaders and shared props must not depend on cookies or other per-visitor state (Netjes warns once per page when a cached render reads `Request.Cookies`). Signed-in users and requests with an `Authorization` header bypass the cache.
- Evict from an action with `ServerAction.Ok().Revalidate("posts")` or `.RevalidatePath("/blog/hello")`, and from anywhere else (a webhook, a background job) with `IPageCache.RevalidateTagAsync(tag)` / `RevalidatePathAsync(path)`.
- Cached pages carry no antiforgery token: forms on them fetch one first, so they need JavaScript.
- A Content-Security-Policy is off unless the app sets one. A document with a CSP nonce is never stored, so cached pages under a policy need a hash-based one (`ContentSecurityPolicy` without `{nonce}`), and under such a policy a page must not stream.
- Keys include the host and the full URL, case included. In production pin `AllowedHosts` and set the output cache's `SizeLimit`.
- Pages the output cache does not store go out `Cache-Control: no-store, private`, for visitors and signed-in users alike, unless the page sets its own header.
- Draft pages and draft redirects (a loader's `Page.Redirect` in draft mode), the client-rendered fallback, the page for a failed form post, action answers and antiforgery tokens always go out `no-store`, and without the headers a CDN reads ahead of `Cache-Control` (`CDN-Cache-Control`, any other `*-Cache-Control`, `Surrogate-Control`, `Edge-Control`, `X-Accel-Expires`), whatever the page set.

## TanStack Query

Netjes creates one `QueryClient` per server render and per page load. `.WithQuery(key, data)` on a loader result seeds it, so `useQuery` with that key has data on the first render and fetches nothing until the data is stale (default `staleTime` one minute). Data the browser fetched more recently is kept. After an action, `.Invalidate(key)` refetches and `.WithQuery(key, data)` sets the new value. Configure the client with `netjes({ query: { defaultOptions } })` in `vite.config.ts`.

## Streaming slow data

```csharp
public sealed record TaskPageProps(TaskDetail Task, Deferred<IReadOnlyList<ActivityItem>> Activity);

app.MapPageLoader("/tasks/[id]", (string id, IDbContextFactory<AppDb> contexts, HttpContext http) =>
    Page.Props(new TaskPageProps(LoadTask(id), Page.Defer(ActivityAsync(contexts, id, http.RequestAborted)))));
```

```tsx
// The generated schema types `activity` as a promise, validated when it arrives (deferred() from netjes/zod).
<Suspense fallback={<p>Loading activity…</p>}>
  <ActivityFeed activity={activity} />
</Suspense>

function ActivityFeed({ activity }: { activity: PromiseLike<ActivityItem[]> }) {
  const items = use(activity);
  return <ol>{items.map((item) => <li key={item.id}>{item.summary}</li>)}</ol>;
}
```

- The shell goes out first, with `loading.tsx` or the Suspense fallback where a value is pending, and each value streams in when its task completes. Client navigations stream the same way.
- A deferred task runs alongside the rest of the request: give it its own `DbContext`, never the request's, and pass `http.RequestAborted`. Either create one from `IDbContextFactory<T>`, as above, or use the overload that runs the work in its own DI scope, started once the page's payload is written: `Page.Defer(services => services.GetRequiredService<AppDb>().ActivityAsync(id, http.RequestAborted))`.
- Without JavaScript, a fallback that is still pending stays. Crawlers (`CrawlerUserAgents`), apps with `StreamDocuments = false` and `netjes export` get the complete document.
- A boundary that is ready when the shell goes out is written in place, so it shows without JavaScript too.

## Static export

`npx netjes export [dir]` builds, runs the app once in Production and writes every page as static HTML (default `out/`). Dynamic pages need `.StaticParams(...)` (`.StaticParams<PostStore>(s => s.All.Select(p => new { slug = p.Slug }))`, arrays for catch-all parameters); pages that need a server take `.ExcludeFromExport()`. The export fails before writing anything for a dynamic page without static params, a page with a page action, or a page that requires authorization. Exported pages navigate with full page loads and carry no antiforgery token.

## Sitemap and robots

`app.MapSitemap(siteUrl)` serves `/sitemap.xml` from the route table (dynamic pages through `.StaticParams`, pages that need authorization or call `.ExcludeFromSitemap()` left out) and `app.MapRobotsTxt(siteUrl, disallow)` serves `/robots.txt`.

Leave `/_netjes/` out of `disallow`: `<Image>` serves every image through `/_netjes/image`, so a crawler that may not fetch it cannot index your images. The other endpoints there take posts or hand out an antiforgery token, which a crawler has no use for. Under a base path, `disallow` paths are written as given, so include the base path in them. See [Metadata](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/metadata.md).

## More

[Caching](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/caching.md), [Rendering and streaming](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/rendering-and-streaming.md) and [Static export](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/static-export.md) in the guides.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/testing.md -->

# Testing

Test first: write the test, watch it fail for the reason you expect, then change the code. Assert what a user or a browser can observe (rendered text, roles, URLs, status codes, the props a page receives), not internals.

## Components and pages: Vitest

`netjes()` in `vite.config.ts` sets up Vitest: jsdom, Testing Library cleanup, and `e2e/`, `dist/`, `bin/` and `obj/` excluded. Tests sit next to the code as `*.test.tsx` and run with `npm test`.

```tsx
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { createTestApp } from 'netjes/testing';
import { expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { HelloForm } from './HelloForm.tsx';

it('shows the validation error from C# next to the field', async () => {
  const app = createTestApp({
    actions: { 'home.greet': () => ({ ok: false, status: 422, errors: { name: ['Tell us your name.'] } }) },
  });
  render(<HelloForm />, { wrapper: app.Wrapper });

  await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Say hello' }));

  expect(await screen.findByText('Tell us your name.')).toBeDefined();
});
```

`createTestApp({ url, params, shared, queries, navigation, antiforgery, actions })` returns `{ Wrapper, navigations, queryClient }`:

- `url` and `params` set what `usePathname`, `useSearchParams` and `useParams` see; `shared` is what `useSharedProps` returns; `queries: [{ key, data }]` seeds TanStack Query as a loader's `.WithQuery` would.
- `actions` answers server action calls by name: `{ ok: true, result }` or `{ ok: false, status: 422, errors }` (add `fields: ['email']` to name the fields a failed state's `values` keep, as the server does). A component that calls an action, even from an effect as it mounts, must render inside `app.Wrapper`: outside it the call fails with "called before the page was ready".
- `navigations` records what happened: `{ type: 'push' | 'replace', href }`, `{ type: 'refresh' | 'back' | 'forward' }`, `{ type: 'submit', action, data }` for form posts, `{ type: 'action', name, input }` for action calls.

Render a page component directly with the props its loader would send: `render(<Post title="Hello" body="..." />, { wrapper: createTestApp({ url: '/blog/hello' }).Wrapper })`. A page made with `definePage` parses them with its schema, so props the loader could not send fail the test with `Invalid props: ...`.

## Loaders and actions: C#

- Loader logic: call the loader or the method it uses and read `PageResult<T>.Props` in an xUnit test.
- Endpoints: test the real app with `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` from `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing` (ASP.NET Core 10 makes the `Program` class of top-level statements public, so the test project sees it). No Node is needed when the test sets `Netjes:Mode` to `Development` (routes come from `app/` on disk) and registers an `ISsrRenderer` (`Netjes.Rendering`) of its own that returns fixed HTML, in `ConfigureServices`. Request a page as the client router does, with the header `X-Netjes-Data: 1` (`NetjesHeaders.Data`): the answer is the page payload as JSON, with `props`, `status` and `antiforgery`; a page with `Page.Defer` values answers NDJSON, the payload first. When the app cannot start (no build in Production, `node` not found), `CreateClient()` throws an `InvalidOperationException` that says why.
- Server actions are `POST /_netjes/actions/{name}`. Call one as the client router does: the fields form-encoded, `X-Netjes-Data: 1`, and the payload's `antiforgery.requestToken` in the header named by `antiforgery.headerName` (a client that keeps cookies, so the antiforgery cookie goes along; `GET /_netjes/antiforgery` returns a token too). A plain form post, as without JavaScript, sends the token as the `antiforgery.formFieldName` field instead.
- Use a real database for data access tests (Testcontainers), not an in-memory fake.

## End to end: Playwright

Put Playwright tests in `e2e/` (Vitest skips it). Run them against the app in Development (`dotnet run --no-launch-profile` with `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development`) and in Production (`npm run build`, then `dotnet run --no-launch-profile` with `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production`), waiting on `/healthz`. Test the forms with JavaScript turned off too (`test.use({ javaScriptEnabled: false })`): they must post, show errors and keep what was typed.

## Before calling a change done

```bash
npm test && npm run typecheck && dotnet build && npx netjes generate --check
```

and `npm run routes` without new warnings.

## More

[Testing](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/testing.md) in the guides, and `createTestApp` in the [React API](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/react-api.md#createtestapp).

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/deployment.md -->

# Deployment

A Netjes app is an ASP.NET Core app that also needs Node at runtime: the .NET process starts and supervises the Node sidecar that renders pages (`NetjesOptions.NodeExecutable`, default `node` on the `PATH`). Only `netjes export` output runs without either.

## Build and publish

```bash
npx netjes generate --check   # in CI: the generated types match the C# types
npm test && npm run typecheck && dotnet build
dotnet publish -c Release -o bin/publish   # runs `npm run build`, ships dist/ (client, server bundle, sidecar)
cd bin/publish && ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production dotnet MyApp.dll
```

`npx netjes start` runs the app in Production from the source tree (or `--dll bin/publish/MyApp.dll`, which runs from the publish folder). In production the routes come from the built client manifest, so a page file that was not built does not exist.

For these startup failures the app logs one critical entry, saying what is wrong and what to do, and exits with code 1: no build in Production (`npm run build`), a `node` it cannot start (`Netjes:NodeExecutable`), a sidecar script that is not installed or built (`npm install` in development, `npm run build` in production), or in development the Vite dev server's port taken, an error in `vite.config.ts` (with Vite's code frame) or a package it imports that is not installed (`npm install`). Under `WebApplicationFactory` the start throws that message instead. Other exceptions at startup, such as a route conflict, keep their stack.

## Docker

`netjes new` writes a `Dockerfile` and Compose files:

- `docker compose up`: development, with `dotnet watch` and Vite HMR, ports bound to localhost.
- `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d`: the production image, a non-root user on a read-only filesystem, with a health check on `/healthz` and Data Protection keys in a named volume.

The image restores Netjes from NuGet and npm, so the app must reference the packages, as an app made with `npx netjes new` does (from a Netjes checkout, pass `--packages`).

## Production settings

- `AllowedHosts`: pin it to the site's host names. `appsettings.Development.json` already limits Development to loopback names.
- HTTPS: outside Development the template calls `UseHsts()` and `UseHttpsRedirection()`. Behind a proxy that terminates TLS, call `UseForwardedHeaders()` first, trusting only that proxy's network (`KnownIPNetworks`), so the app sees https and the visitor's address.
- Data Protection keys sign antiforgery tokens and draft-mode cookies: keep them across restarts (the production compose file mounts a volume) and share them between instances.
- Several instances behind a load balancer also share the output-cache store and need the same `Netjes:SegmentKeySecret` (32 bytes or more).
- `Netjes:SidecarProcesses`: Node processes rendering in production (default 1; about one per core for CPU-heavy pages).
- If no sidecar is ready (they crashed and are restarting), documents are sent for the browser to render instead of failing (`ClientRenderFallback`, on by default), and `/healthz` reports Unhealthy. Register the check with `builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().AddNetjes()` and `app.MapHealthChecks("/healthz")`.
- Output caching: set `SizeLimit`, and see [caching-and-streaming.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/caching-and-streaming.md).
- Security headers: every document gets `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` and a same-origin framing policy unless the app sets them (`Netjes:SecurityHeaders`). A Content-Security-Policy is off until you set `NetjesOptions.ContentSecurityPolicy`, with `{nonce}` for a nonce-based policy.
- `Netjes:PublicConfig` is sent to the browser as is; secrets go in other configuration.
- Telemetry: add the `Netjes` ActivitySource and Meter (`NetjesTelemetry.Name`) to OpenTelemetry for loader, action and render spans and render durations.

## Startup work and CLI commands

`netjes generate` and `netjes routes` run the app once in command mode, without serving or starting Node. Skip startup work they do not need, such as migrations or seeding:

```csharp
if (app.GetNetjesCommand() is null)
{
    await SeedAsync(app.Services);
}
```

## Static hosting

`npx netjes export` writes the site as static HTML to `out/` for any static host; see [caching-and-streaming.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/packages/netjes/skills/netjes/references/caching-and-streaming.md#static-export) for what it needs and refuses.

## More

[Deployment](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/deployment.md) and [Security](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/guides/security.md) in the guides, and every option in [Options](https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/blob/main/docs/reference/options.md).

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/README.md -->

# Design decisions

These records explain why Netjes is built the way it is, for contributors and for anyone weighing it against another framework. Each one states a decision, the context that led to it, the alternatives considered and what follows from it. [The architecture page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/architecture.md) describes how the pieces fit together; these records say why they are those pieces.

- [0001 – React renders in a pool of Node sidecars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0001-react-renders-in-node-sidecars.md): supervised Node processes render React, and .NET balances renders between them.
- [0002 – The server owns routing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0002-server-owns-routing.md): routes are matched in C# only, and the client router asks the server for every page.
- [0003 – React renders the whole document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0003-react-renders-the-whole-document.md): React renders `<html>` itself, head and metadata included.
- [0004 – Vite for the dev server and builds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0004-vite-for-dev-server-and-builds.md): Vite serves modules in development and builds the client and server bundles.
- [0005 – A small default stack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0005-a-small-default-stack.md): React, TanStack Query, Tailwind CSS and Vitest, with no other runtime dependencies.
- [0006 – Types and zod schemas generated from the C# contracts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0006-types-and-zod-from-csharp-contracts.md): the running app writes `generated/netjes.ts` from its System.Text.Json contracts.
- [0007 – A Node CLI in the npm package, which asks the app itself](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0007-a-node-cli-that-asks-the-app.md): `netjes` runs the app in command mode to report its routes and types.
- [0008 – Image processing is pluggable, SkiaSharp optional](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0008-pluggable-image-processing.md): the image endpoint owns the rules, and a separate package resizes.
- [0009 – Public configuration is sent at runtime](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0009-public-config-at-runtime.md): `Netjes:PublicConfig` reaches the browser with the first document, not through the build.
- [0010 – The App Router's conventions, with C# layout loaders instead of server components](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0010-app-router-with-csharp-layout-loaders.md): `app/` only, and each segment's data comes from C#.
- [0011 – Server actions are C# endpoints with typed references](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0011-server-actions-as-csharp-endpoints.md): stable names, antiforgery and origin checks, and forms that work without JavaScript.
- [0012 – Streamed documents, deferred values, and ready boundaries in place](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0012-streamed-documents-and-deferred-values.md): documents stream, `Page.Defer` values follow the shell, and ready boundaries need no script.
- [0013 – A client-rendered fallback when no sidecar is ready](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0013-client-rendered-fallback.md): .NET sends the payload for the browser to render while Node is down.
- [0014 – Signing in or out clears what Back shows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0014-signing-in-or-out-clears-what-back-shows.md): a cookie change in an action makes the router and the browser forget pages.
- [0015 – Route warnings name what is likely wrong, not everything that could be](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0015-route-warnings-name-what-is-likely-wrong.md): startup warnings for query-bound loader parameters and overlapping pages.
- [0016 – Page cache rules under any output caching](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0016-page-cache-rules-under-any-output-caching.md): page keys, tags and token rules apply whatever policy caches a page.
- [0017 – A form input without any of its fields is empty, not null](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0017-a-form-input-without-fields-is-empty-not-null.md): an action gets an empty `[FromForm]` input, checked like any other, where form binding gives none.
- [0018 – A startup failure that says what to do ends the app in one line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0018-startup-failures-end-in-one-line.md): a missing build, Node.js or Vite dev server is one log entry and exit code 1, and a failed start in a test host.
- [0019 – A forced no-store removes the headers CDNs read first](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0019-forced-no-store-removes-cdn-cache-headers.md): drafts, the fallback and the other `no-store` responses go out without `CDN-Cache-Control`, `Surrogate-Control` and the like.
- [0020 – Page actions check their inputs like server actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0020-page-actions-check-their-inputs-like-server-actions.md): a failed check renders the page again from its loader, and `usePageActionState()` reads it.
- [0021 – Signing in or out reaches the app's other tabs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0021-signing-in-or-out-reaches-the-other-tabs.md): a tab that sees a cookie change tells the others on a `BroadcastChannel`, and they forget and reload the same way.

A decision that a newcomer would not guess, or that was chosen over a real alternative, gets a new record with the next number. An accepted record is not rewritten when the decision changes; a new record supersedes it.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/CHANGELOG.md -->

# Changelog

All notable changes to Netjes are recorded here: the `netjes` npm package and the `Netjes` and `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp` NuGet packages, which are released together under one version. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Before 1.0, a new version can change the API; its entry says what to do.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.0.1] - 2026-10-30

Initial release.

### Added

- **Routing.** Pages in `app/` with the Next.js App Router conventions: `page`, `layout`, `template`, `loading`, `error`, `not-found`, `forbidden`, `unauthorized` and `global-error` files, route groups, private folders, dynamic, catch-all and optional catch-all segments, and parallel and intercepting routes. Each page is an ASP.NET Core endpoint, so the matcher, `RequireAuthorization()` and other endpoint conventions apply. Route warnings at startup and in `netjes routes` for loader parameters that miss a route value, for pages that match the same URLs, and for form inputs that refuse a post without a checkbox.
- **Client router.** `<Link>` with prefetching, `useRouter`, `usePathname`, `useSearchParams` and `useParams` with optional schemas, `useSelectedLayoutSegment(s)`, `useNavigation`, scroll restoration, and back and forward from memory for the last 50 pages. Base paths (`UsePathBase` with `netjes({ basePath })`) and locale routing on a `[lang]` segment (`AddNetjesLocalization`, `useLocale`).
- **Data loading.** C# page loaders (`MapPageLoader`) and layout loaders (`MapLayoutLoader`) that bind like minimal API handlers and return `Page.Props`, `NotFound`, `Forbidden`, `Unauthorized`, `Redirect` or `LocalRedirect`. Layout loaders are skipped on navigations within their section, keyed by signed segment keys. Shared props for every page (`UseSharedProps`), public configuration read at runtime (`Netjes:PublicConfig`, `usePublicConfig`), and a built-in TanStack Query client seeded from loaders with `.WithQuery`.
- **Generated types.** `generated/netjes.ts`, written from the app's System.Text.Json contracts: zod schemas for page and layout props, shared props, JSON endpoints and page action forms, typed server action references, typed routes (`route()`, `Href`), and `definePage` and `defineLayout` to parse props with them. `netjes generate --check` for CI.
- **Server actions and forms.** `MapAction` endpoints with typed references, `useAction` and `<Form>`, DataAnnotations and `IValidatableObject` validation, `ServerAction.Ok`, `Invalid`, `Redirect`, `Forbidden` and `NotFound`, revalidation of cached pages and refreshes, TanStack Query updates, and page actions (`MapPageAction`), whose inputs are validated the same way, with the errors in `usePageActionState`. Forms post without JavaScript and come back with their errors and the declared fields' values. Antiforgery and same-origin checks on every action, a 1 MB body limit for server actions, and a refresh of the router's memory and query cache, in every tab of the app, when an action signs someone in or out.
- **Rendering.** Server rendering in a pool of supervised Node processes (`SidecarProcesses`), restarted with backoff and reported by a health check. Streamed documents with `loading.tsx` and Suspense, `Page.Defer` for slow values (with an overload that runs the work in its own DI scope), ready boundaries written in place, complete documents for crawlers, and a document the browser renders itself when no Node process is ready in production. `dynamic()`, `clientOnly()`, error pages and built-in fallbacks.
- **Caching.** `.CachePage(duration, tags)` on ASP.NET Core output caching, with Netjes's keys under any output-cache policy; revalidation by tag or path from actions or through `IPageCache`; draft mode (`IDraftMode`, `useDraftMode`) that bypasses the cache. Pages that are not cached go out `no-store`.
- **Metadata, images and scripts.** The Metadata API on pages and layouts and `PageMetadata` from C#, `MapSitemap` and `MapRobotsTxt`, `<Script>` with three loading strategies, and `<Image>` with the `/_netjes/image` endpoint: configured widths and qualities, allow-listed remote hosts, bounded concurrency, and a pluggable `IImageProcessor`. `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp` resizes and encodes WebP.
- **Static export.** `netjes export` writes every page as a complete HTML document, with `.StaticParams(...)` for dynamic pages and `.ExcludeFromExport()`, and refuses pages that need a server.
- **Security.** `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` and a same-origin framing policy on every document, an opt-in Content-Security-Policy with per-request nonces or hashes, redirects limited to relative and http(s) URLs, form fields that look like secrets never handed back, and a token on every request to the Node processes.
- **Operations.** The `Netjes` ActivitySource and Meter for OpenTelemetry (loader, action, render and sidecar spans and durations, web vitals with `netjes/vitals`), a health check, and support for several instances sharing an output-cache store.
- **Testing.** Vitest defaults in the Vite plugin and `createTestApp()` from `netjes/testing`, with a fake router, seeded queries and fake server actions.
- **Tooling.** The `netjes` command: `new`, `dev`, `build`, `start`, `generate`, `routes`, `export`, `info` and `agents`. An app template with a C# loader, a validated server action, component tests, Tailwind CSS and Docker files for development and production. `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and a Netjes skill for coding agents in new apps, and `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` for the docs. The npm package ships compiled ES modules with type declarations.

[Unreleased]: https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/compare/v0.0.1...HEAD
[0.0.1]: https://github.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/releases/tag/v0.0.1

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/roadmap.md -->

# Roadmap

The work in progress, what comes next, what is planned without a date, and what is left out by design. Nothing here is a promise: plans change as people use Netjes and report what they need. To ask for something, or to say that an item matters to you, open a discussion or an issue on GitHub.

## Now

- **The 0.0.1 release.** The packages `netjes` on npm and `Netjes` and `Netjes.Images.SkiaSharp` on NuGet, released together under one version, with the documentation, `llms.txt` and the app template.

## Next

- **Apps without Node in production.** An option to render every page in the browser, from the client-rendered document Netjes already serves while no Node process is ready, so an app runs on .NET alone. Loaders, actions, typed props and client navigation keep working. What goes is what server rendering gives: HTML for crawlers and link previews, the metadata in that HTML, forms that work before the JavaScript loads, and caching of documents (a client-rendered document goes out `no-store`; data payloads can still be cached). It revisits [ADR 0001](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0001-react-renders-in-node-sidecars.md), which chose server rendering, so it starts with a new decision record.
- **Instant loading.** On a client navigation, show the target's `loading.tsx` at once inside the layouts it shares with the current page, then stream in the layout loaders' props and the page as they are ready, instead of waiting for the whole payload.
- **Caching depth.** Stale-while-revalidate for cached pages, cache profiles, tags added by a loader at render time, revalidation by route pattern or layout, and a cached shell that is filled for an anonymous visitor, for pages with a part that differs per visitor.
- **Metadata and images.** The metadata file conventions in `app/` (`icon`, `apple-icon`, `opengraph-image`, `twitter-image`, `manifest`), generated Open Graph images, richer sitemaps and `robots.txt`, `metadataBase` and `viewport`, and more of `<Image>`: `fill`, blur placeholders and static imports.
- **Client navigation in static exports.** Write each page's payload next to its HTML, so exported sites navigate without full page loads, with a trailing-slash option, the sitemap and `robots.txt` in the export, and images resized at export time.
- **Bundle size.** Smaller first-load JavaScript: generated schemas split per route and free of side effects, so bundlers can drop what a page does not use, and `dynamic()` chunks preloaded from the build manifest.
- **Error handling.** An id for each server error, logged with the exception and shown to the user, a way to retry the failed segment from `error.tsx`, and a global error boundary in the browser.
- **Internationalisation.** Redirects from paths without a locale, `hreflang` alternates from the supported cultures, and optional domains per locale.
- **Operations.** Streamed responses that proxies do not buffer, an asset prefix for serving the client build from a CDN, a deployment id, and letting renders in progress finish when a Node process is stopped.

## Later

- Partial prerendering: a cached HTML shell, resumed by React with the parts that differ per request.
- valibot as an alternative to zod in the generated file.
- Navigations that keep what an unmatched parallel-route slot showed, as Next.js does after a soft navigation.
- A `__Host-` antiforgery cookie by default. It is an opt-in today for apps served only over HTTPS: as a default it would break plain-HTTP development and `UsePathBase`.
- `<Link>` treating `/x` and `/x/` as the same page for `aria-current`.
- AVIF output for `<Image>`, from a second image processor.
- Typegen edge cases: item nullability for collection subclasses (`class Tags : List<string?>`), `UnknownDerivedTypeHandling.FallBackToBaseType` in discriminated unions, and read semantics (defaulted properties optional, computed ones left out) for JSON endpoint request schemas, as server action inputs have.

## Not planned

Netjes leaves these out by design. Taking one up would need a new decision record that supersedes the one named.

- React Server Components. C# loaders do their job: data comes from C# as props, and every component ships to the browser ([ADR 0010](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0010-app-router-with-csharp-layout-loaders.md)).
- The pages router, and its hooks for code moving from `pages/`: `useRouter().query`, `asPath`, router events and shallow routing ([ADR 0010](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0010-app-router-with-csharp-layout-loaders.md)).
- Serverless and edge hosts. Pages render in long-lived Node processes next to the .NET app ([ADR 0001](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DennisVerhoeven/netjes/main/docs/decisions/0001-react-renders-in-node-sidecars.md)).
